long_desc: Surrounded by a timber palisade with North, South, West, and East Gates and bisected by the willow-lined Dragon Canal, the Human Village is the bustling heart of human civilization in Gensokyo. Protected by Keine Kamishirasawa and chronicled by the Hieda clan, its four-block Main Street hosts morning markets at 07:00 and locks down when the watchman's copper curfew bell rings at 20:00.

wiki_summary:
The Human Village (人間の里, Ningen no Sato) is a Meiji era themed village where most of Gensokyo's humans live. Even though some youkai also visit here to shop, this is the safest place in all of Gensokyo to live. Humans from the outside world that stumble into Gensokyo and decide to stay often have no choice but to live here as they would be unable to handle the youkai outside the village. The Human Village is the main setting of Forbidden Scrollery and Lotus Eaters.

[Inhabitants]
The village is moderated by the Tengu and Kappa but also watched over by the Youkai Sages. The newspapers from Crow Tengu are distributed to humans in the village while the Kappa tend to create inventions or have markets in the village as well. Keine Kamishirasawa is a teacher within the village who is very knowledgeable about it's history and capable of "hiding" the history of the village's existence for its protection. Other important residents are Hieda no Akyuu who is a chronicler of Gensokyo, Kosuzu Motoori who rents out books in Suzunaan, Miyoi Okunoda who is a poster girl of Geidontei, and Marisa Kirisame's parents who also still live in the village. Marisa's father also owns the Kirisame-ya second-hand shop. Some stores stay open late into the night to cater exclusively to youkai. Geidontei is one of those stores. Some households within the village may possess resident zashiki-warashi, who are adored by humans but secretly act as spies for the Youkai Sages. They were briefly replaced by hofgoblins during the events of Wild and Horned Hermit, who failed to achieve the same level of popularity.

According to Rinnosuke Morichika, some human residents also study magic or other esoteric arts. Humans from the village who try to become Youkai, or a Jinyou may be exterminated by the current shrine maiden of Gensokyo such as Reimu Hakurei. The humans of the village rely on Reimu to protect the village and may travel to the Hakurei Shrine to pray to gods or to attend other events. Other inhabitants consist of an unnamed leader who has a son, a florist, a woodcutter, a teahouse, a tofu shop, youkai exterminators, and more. In the recent past, a secret society was rumored to have existed, intending to learn secrets from research into the beginnings of human and youkai residence in Gensokyo with a goal of asserting human control and expelling youkai from the land.

wiki_summary:
is a traditional Japanese style book renter located somewhere in the Human Village. Although it is a book renter, they also sell books, and even provide a small book printing service. The Gensokyo Chronicle (Perfect Memento in Strict Sense) written by Hieda no Akyuu was also printed and bound here.

Most of the books they deal in are the books that drifted into Gensokyo from the outside world, which they call "foreign books" (外来本, gairai bon). Kosuzu has been also secretly using some income of the store to gather a collection of rare demon books, and rents out at high price.

The inspiration of this shop is [http://www.norinagakinenkan.com/collect/syosai30.html Suzunoya] lit. "Floor of Bell" (鈴屋), the personal study room of Norinaga Motoori, who is very likely the inspiration of Kosuzu. And you can find a mark of something like vegetable on the store curtains, name board of the shop, and even the font of title logo. Those are all turnips, which are called in a little old Japanese "suzuna" (/) — the latter literally means "bell vegetable" to resemble the shape of bell and turnip. This might be referred from [http://www.norinagakinenkan.com/norinaga/kaisetsu/onraizu.html "Illustration of Thanks-to" (恩頼図, Onraizu)], drawn after Norinaga's death by one of his disciples. The words which Norinaga had relation of are arranged in a shape of turnip, in order to express what he was — in other words, the turnip means Norinaga himself on the illustration.

long_desc: Fed by mountain runoff from Genbu Ravine, this stone-lined canal bisects the Human Village before winding outward beneath weeping willows. Peaceful by day, its shadowy embankments become haunted by nocturnal apparitions and tsurube-otoshi after the 20:00 curfew bell.

wiki_summary:
The Canal of Willows (柳の運河, Yanagi no Unga) is a canal near the Human Village, where willow trees can be found. It is presented as a vaguely ominous location, though in actuality, the heroine seems genuinely surprised to find that there are actually youkai running rampant there after so many years, implying that it is supposedly intended to be peaceful.

As the name implies, it is a water canal strewn with willows, and due to its close proximity to the Human Village, as well as the in-game assumption that rampaging youkai wouldn't be near it, it can be safely assumed that it serves a regular purpose for the village and that humans visit it frequently. In spite of the heroines' assumptions, however, Sekibanki implies that several youkai do in fact come to the canal as well, and that like herself, some even reside in the Human Village, presenting themselves as humans. The title of Double Dealing Character Stage 2's theme song, "Humans and Youkai, Coming and Going at the Canal", seems to corroborate this assertion.

Sekibanki herself, of course, can also be found roaming about here now and then. Marisa Kirisame does also state that "the seats under the the willows" have a reputation as being the homes of phantoms.

Night sparrow Mystia Lorelei pitches her warm red-lantern yatai here to serve freshly grilled lamprey to humans and youkai alike.

wiki_summary:
The Youkai Trail (妖怪獣道, Yōkai Kemonomichi) is a narrowed path that, on one end, should lead to the Human Village. Mystia Lorelei is known to lurk around here.

Little is known about this location. According to Sakuya Izayoi, this place has beauty that she didn't know because she travels here at night. The road tends to lack humans, because it is infested with youkai, in particular beast-types. Even though it's a road for youkai, the end of it doesn't have youkai due to being close to the village. Mystia Lorelei states that humans who do come here are "idiots".

Apparently, Mystia has a stand set up here that sells Grilled Lamprey. She tricks bypassers into thinking that this food will cure their night-blindness, although it is Mystia that's causing this herself.

It was a stage location in Hopeless Masquerade and Urban Legend in Limbo that's associated with Mamizou Futatsuiwa. There is also a night version of this stage. On that stage, there appears to be open space, with having trees behind the scenery.

short_desc: Byakuren Hijiri's pacifist Buddhist temple located a 10-minute walk southwest of the Human Village.
long_desc: Formed when the flying Palanquin Ship landed near the Human Village, Myouren Temple is a serene Buddhist monastery dedicated to peaceful coexistence between humans and youkai. Under High Priestess Byakuren Hijiri, its swept courtyards host daytime sermons, festivals, and shelter for repentant monsters.
placement_note: South-southwest outskirts of the Human Village (6-10 min walk from the South/West Gates).
wiki_summary:
The Myouren Temple (, also the Palanquin Ship ( or Treasure Ship Above the Clouds (雲上の宝船, Unjō no Takarabune), was originally a ship capable of sailing through the sky, where it was landed directly on top of the Hall of Dreams' Great Mausoleum and renovated into a temple. In its original ship form, it was capable of traveling to Makai. The temple can still transform back into its ship form whenever Byakuren Hijiri chooses to.

The inspiration for the Palanquin Ship is the flying warehouse (飛倉, Tobi Kura), which appears in the first volume of Shigi san Engi Emaki. The story goes that Myouren made a bowl fly, so it was called the Flying Bowl (飛鉢, Hihatsu), for people to place offerings into. When a certain rich man suspected that Myouren might be skimming off the top, he shut the bowl in a closed storehouse. In return, Myouren made the whole storehouse fly, along with the bowl and the other stored supplies like bales of rice. The rich man asked Myouren to give back the supplies, so he did. After a long time, perhaps after long time passed since Myouren died, the Flying Storehouse fell into ruin, but it gained sacred power from his cloth which his sister gave to him. People wondered about it, so they removed pieces of it from the Storehouse.

The Palanquin Ship's name in Japanese is pronounced "Seirensen", identical to the Japanese title of Undefined Fantastic Object. The kanji on the sail is "", an archaic version of "" meaning "treasure".

approach_route: Exit the Human Village gate toward the curved grey-tiled Palanquin Ship roof rising above the trees; connects west through a stone torii to Myouren Temple Cemetery and east past Kogasa's Forge along the scenic footpath loop to Kourindou.
local_customs: Pacifist Buddhist sanctuary led by Byakuren Hijiri where humans and youkai coexist peacefully; safe daytime refuge.

long_desc: Located two minutes west down the stone steps of Myouren Temple along the hillside path toward the Hakurei Shrine road, this old cemetery is lined with weathered stupas and stone lanterns. Kogasa Tatara practices ambushing visitors here at dawn, while Jiangshi guard Yoshika Miyako patrols the hidden entrance to the Hall of Dreams beneath the tombs.

wiki_summary:
The Myouren Temple Cemetery (命蓮寺墓地, Myourenji bochi) is a cemetery, as its name suggest, found near the Myouren Temple. The Cemetery is very old and may possibly have been part of the Hall of Dreams' Great Mausoleum and was either built before or after it.cn It appears as though the cemetery is currently under the property of Myouren Temple itself, as the name suggests.

Not much is actually known about the cemetery. Just like any other cemetery however, it is full of gravestones. They appear to be under cherry blossom trees, and incense's smoke can be seen coming out of some of the gravestones. Yoshika Miyako, a jiang shi controlled by Seiga Kaku, appeared here during Ten Desires to try and chase away the intruding heroines from the Hall of Dreams' Great Mausoleum. It is unknown if she still lurks here, but she was shown here as of Impossible Spell Card. Kogasa Tatara also seems to lurk around here, exploiting the creepiness of the cemetery to scare people, since she finds it easier to surprise people here.

long_desc: Situated in a vast underground cavern directly beneath Myouren Temple (which was intentionally placed atop it as a Buddhist seal), this palatial mausoleum was the resurrection chamber of Crown Prince Toyosatomimi no Miko. Its subterranean halls connect directly via spatial portal to the hermit pocket dimension of Senkai.

wiki_summary:

The Hall of Dreams' Great Mausoleum (夢殿大祀廟, Yumedono Daishibyou) lies directly underneath the Myouren Temple, and is the setting of stage 4, 5 and 6 of Ten Desires. Within the Myouren Temple Cemetery next to the temple lies a cave, which leads to the Mausoleum. It holds many spirits such as Soga no Tojiko.

Further inside lies the Divine Spirit Mausoleum (神霊廟, Shinreibyō), in which the tomb of Toyosatomimi no Miko is located, but it's presumed that the temple was later re-located to Senkai based on details from Hopeless Masquerade.

In the past, Miko's mausoleum was constantly sealed by Buddhists preventing her from resurrecting. As time passed legends like Toyosatomimi no Miko faded away transporting her mausoleum and everyone within it to Gensokyo.

The Buddhist monk Byakuren Hijiri's Myouren Temple originally was settled on top of where Toyosatomimi no Miko's mausoleum was located; as a saint of humans, the two would naturally be at odds. This choice ended up causing the seal to be broken. In Reimu's ending and Sanae's alternate ending of Ten Desires, because they were opposed to living in a place under a temple of youkai, Toyosatomimi and her followers relocated to a dōjō in another world called Senkai. 

As of Hopeless Masquerade, Miko had constructed a Taoist temple within Senkai known as the Divine Spirit Mausoleum (神霊廟). It welcomes humans aspiring to become hermits, but most of them fail the necessary training. It shares its name with the area in Stage 6 of Ten Desires. Based on Futo's Ending in Hopeless Masquerade, while not specifically called a Senkai, Miko and Futo's realm are described as "a space created by hermit arts, it's unclear if it's actually in Gensokyo." is extremely similar to the other descriptions of Senkai.

Miko and her followers were also shown residing in Senkai in Wild and Horned Hermit Chapter 18.
The Hall of Dreams' Great Mausoleum is based on the wikipedia:Hōryū-ji#Yumedono (Hall of Dreams) (Hall of Dreams, 夢殿) of Houryuu-ji. It stands in a half area of the temple, Touin (東院, lit. "Eastern Yard"), and the other area is Sai'in (西院, lit. "Western Yard"). In the Hall of Dreams, there is Guze Kannon, which is said to have the same height as Prince Shoutoku, who Toyosatomimi no Miko is based on.

long_desc: Created by Taoist hermits to escape the cramped underground caverns beneath Myouren Temple, Senkai is an expansive pocket dimension of perpetual clear skies, plum blossoms, and training pavilions. Toyosatomimi no Miko and her retainers relocated their primary residence here after their resurrection.

wiki_summary: Senkai (仙界) is a sealed secret world suited for hermits, which even Gensokyo did not know of before the events of Ten Desires. According to Toyosatomimi no Miko during the first part of a symposium between her, Kanako Yasaka and Byakuren Hijiri, it's a space that Miko had created, herself. A location where nobody else can bother someone is well-suited for hermits.

approach_route: Descend into the Hall of Dreams' Great Mausoleum beneath Myouren Temple and step through the Taoist spatial gate into the sunlit hermit realm.
local_customs: Sovereign hermit training realm of Toyosatomimi no Miko; inaccessible without a Taoist resident's permission.

short_desc: Reimu Hakurei's border shrine perched on the western mountain ridge overlooking all of Gensokyo.
long_desc: Standing at the very edge of the Great Hakurei Barrier a 20-minute uphill climb west-northwest from the Human Village, the Hakurei Shrine maintains the boundary between Gensokyo and the Outside World. Though chronically short on human worshippers and offertory coins, its swept veranda is the prime gathering spot for youkai, sages, and incident resolvers.
placement_note: Elevated border hilltop 20 minutes uphill WNW of the Human Village West Gate, overlooking the central Gensokyo basin.
wiki_summary:
The Hakurei Shrine (博麗神社, Hakurei Jinja) is a small, dilapidated Shinto shrine located on the Great Hakurei Barrier on the eastern edge of Gensokyo. It's a key location that has appeared in many of the official games' prologues, stages, in character endings and in other official literature by ZUN. It's the home of the Touhou Project's protagonist: Reimu Hakurei.

The shrine has become a popular hangout for all sorts of youkai who Reimu and company defeat in the course of the games. However, because of this, very few (normal) humans come to the shrine, and even fewer (if any at all) leave donations, but because it is a place where human faith gathers, Aunn Komano tends to guard the place without being asked.

The Hakurei Shrine was once the only shrine in Gensokyo, but the Moriya Shrine has since settled on the Youkai Mountain. Also adding to religious competition is the Myouren Temple and the Hall of Dreams' Great Mausoleum; the former is a Buddhist temple led by Byakuren Hijiri and the latter is held by Taoists run by Toyosatomimi no Miko‎.

From Wild and Horned Hermit chapter 8, it's known that there is money scattered around the shrine. Although the ones found by Reimu may have been planted there by the Unnamed Kuda-gitsune. It's later seen that like all shrines, the Hakurei Shrine offers omamori. Although with the Hakurei Shrine's god in question, it's unknown if the omamori would even provide anyone with divine power.

travel_time: ~20 minutes uphill walk on foot from the Human Village West Gate (~15 minutes downhill return to the village).
approach_route: Exit the Human Village West Gate -> follow the maintained open-ground road west-northwest -> climb the moss-grown Lower Stone Steps through the faded red torii gate to the shrine porch. (Note: the Scarlet Devil Mansion is visible across the basin from this hill only in autumn when lake mist thins; the shrine cannot be seen from the SDM).
local_customs: Reimu Hakurei's sovereign border sanctuary; safe during daylight, but travelers must return before the 20:00 curfew bell as border youkai hunt along the road at dusk.

short_desc: The metaphysical boundary of common sense and unreality enveloping Gensokyo behind the Hakurei Shrine.
long_desc: Erected in 1885 by the Sages of Gensokyo and the Hakurei clan, the Great Hakurei Barrier divides the forgotten supernatural world inside from scientific modern Japan outside. Behind the Hakurei Shrine's main hall, the physical seam of the barrier hums with visible spiritual discharge.
placement_note: Five minutes uphill west behind the Hakurei Shrine along the western border ridge.
wiki_summary: The Great Hakurei Barrier (博麗大結界, Hakurei Dai-Kekkai) is the barrier that hides Gensokyo away from the Outside World, and which allows youkai to survive within even when outside humans no longer believe in them. It is known that the Hakurei Shrine is located on the border and believed that Yukari Yakumo lives somewhere along the border as well (though not near the shrine).

travel_time: ~25 minutes uphill west from the Human Village West Gate (5 minutes past the Hakurei Shrine main hall).
approach_route: Climb the Hakurei Shrine stone steps and pass behind the main shrine building to the boundary ridge where the barrier seam hums with spiritual pressure.
local_customs: Regulated exclusively by Reimu Hakurei and Barrier Sage Yukari Yakumo; unilateral crossing without a Sage gap or shrine ritual is impossible.

long_desc: A quiet, crimson-carpeted footpath running along the western border between the woods and Muenzuka. Clustered with poisonous red spider lilies (higanbana), the trail takes its name from how despondent outsiders who wash through the barrier reconsider their lives as they walk back toward the Human Village.
placement_note: Western border trail linking the forest edge and Hakurei ridge to Muenzuka.
wiki_summary:
The Road of Reconsideration (再思の道, Saishi no michi) is a road where the red spider lilies blooms (especially in the autumn season, dyeing the road a deep red), connecting the Forest of Magic and Muenzuka. Avoided by the humans of Gensokyo due to its distant location, the Great Hakurei Barrier is somewhat blurred here.

The threat level is 'high' and phantoms and ghost are easily encountered, as well as an outsider is also likely. Many humans of Gensokyo never approach here, for the reason that opening to the Outside World could happen at any time; same goes for the Netherworld, as this is a place where several barriers overlap and intersect. Those without relatives and those who try to commit suicide in the Outside World will often end up drifting across this road, ending up at Muenzuka. As those who've tried to commit suicide walk along this path when it is covered with red spider lilies, the toxins will swirl around their bodies, and then something wondrous yet unpleasant takes place: their will to survive will become rejuvenated. And then, deciding to try once more, they will suddenly come to reconsider their decisions and turn back with a renewed will to live. This is why this road has been called the "Road of Reconsideration".

There are nasty youkai who lie in wait, hoping to hunt for a meal of an outsider. After going through the trouble of enduring the struggles of reconsideration, and just when thinking about once again trying their best, being preyed upon by a youkai is no suitable repayment or reward. Depressed people, spiteful people bearing grudges, criminals and the like are the favorite food of youkai. There are plenty of those kinds of people here.
atlas_sector: Western Border Trail linking the Forest of Magic's western edge to Muenzuka.
travel_time: ~35–45 minutes walk southwest from the Human Village via the Forest of Magic border (~15 minutes walk end-to-end to Muenzuka).
approach_route: Skirt the western edge of the Forest of Magic along the quiet trail carpeted with blooming red spider lilies (higanbana) leading straight into Muenzuka.
local_customs: Unpatrolled liminal border path; travelers lingering among the spider lilies risk melancholic disorientation and wandering spirits.

short_desc: Poisonous spider-lily hollow at the Great Hakurei Barrier where Outside World drift goods and the forgotten dead gather.
long_desc: Located at the western terminus of the Road of Reconsideration where the Great Hakurei Barrier thins, Muenzuka is an unmarked graveyard for those without relatives. Because the boundary between worlds is weakest here, obsolete electronics, scrap metal, and lost outsiders frequently wash ashore amid the toxic purple-and-crimson lilies.
placement_note: Far western border hollow at the end of the Road of Reconsideration, overlooking the central Gensokyo basin.
wiki_summary:
Muenzuka (無縁塚) is a small, wooded area located at the end of the Road of Reconsideration, known for its poisonous, deep red-colored red spider lilies. It is the graveyard of humans who don't have relatives (and are usually from outside Gensokyo). Many treasures from the Outside World make their way to Gensokyo by floating here.

Muenzuka is the resting place for the nameless dead. In Gensokyo, where human corpses are not neglected due to the youkai, the nameless corpses are cremated and laid to rest here. Because it is a place for the dead, and because humans quite often become phantoms after death, it is quite close to the Netherworld, as well as the Outside World. Normally, the barriers do not intersect, but that is happening here. For this reason, maintaining one's presence within one realm is difficult. However, apparently people are known to appear here from the Outside World as well, happening to fall into it by chance. It is also the home of purple cherry blossom trees, some of the most beautiful flower in Gensokyo. When the flowers of these cherry blossoms fall, the deceased of Muenzuka will be released from their hesitation and will finally progress to the Road of Liminality.

The purple cherry blossoms purify the soil of Muenzuka, and once per year, bloom to sever all hesitation. Even for Gensokyo, these are quite peculiar youkai cherry trees. Those flower petals that drop by ones and twos create a sight reminiscent of Muenzuka itself weeping, an illusion that will beguile any viewer. This might be the most perfect place for flower viewing, or so one might think, but the sorrowful sights create such sadness that there is no one who is able to make merry while watching them.

Nazrin is known to live in a little hut she built near Muenzuka, in search of treasure. In addition, Rinnosuke Morichika is known to go there often to collect goods for his shop Kourindou. Despite being a small area enclosed by trees, it is known to be one of the most dangerous place in Gensokyo for both the humans and youkai.
It is named after a Japanese Buddhist term "muen-botoke" (無縁仏), meaning "a dead person or soul lacking their relatives by blood and marriage who arrange their grave".
atlas_sector: Far Western Border Hollow (drift hollow at the terminus of the Road of Reconsideration against the Great Hakurei Barrier).
travel_time: ~50–60 minutes walk west-southwest from the Human Village (or ~30 minutes west from the Forest of Magic via the Road of Reconsideration).
approach_route: Branch southwest from the Hakurei Shrine border footpath, or follow the red spider-lily-lined Road of Reconsideration west from the Forest of Magic into the wooded hollow.
local_customs: Unprotected border graveyard choked with poisonous red spider lilies where Outside World drift goods and lost outsiders wash ashore; lethal hazard for unescorted humans.

short_desc: Rinnosuke Morichika's cluttered curio shop standing on the exact border between the Human Village road and the Forest of Magic.
long_desc: A solitary, Western-accented timber storehouse located a 20–30 minute walk south-southeast of the Human Village at the threshold of the Forest of Magic. Proprietor Rinnosuke Morichika uses his ability to discern the names and purposes of Outside World artifacts, though his cluttered shelves rarely see paying customers.
placement_note: Northern edge of the Forest of Magic along the southern road from the Human Village.
wiki_summary:
Kourindou (香霖堂) is an antique store seated between the Human Village and the Forest of Magic, run by Rinnosuke Morichika.

The store is Rinnosuke's home. Although it's a somewhat well-known establishment for the residents of Gensokyo, Rinnosuke rarely (if ever) actually sells anything, despite keeping an exhaustive inventory; he mostly trades and/or puts up with "creative borrowing" from Reimu Hakurei and Marisa Kirisame. The store doesn't get very many customers aside from the usual noisy ones. Mold often grows in the store, as well, which may contribute to this.

On occasion, the store is used for completely non-business ventures, such as cooking and combat. The store has also taken quite a bit of damage over time, thanks to conflicts that involve the store's occupants.

The inventory of Kourindou is (presumably) its main draw, as it mostly includes items from the outside world. Teacups, feather pillows, computing magazines, kerosene/paraffin heaters, and even an iPod have made their way there over time.
atlas_sector: South-Southeast Forest Threshold (at the exact northern edge of the Forest of Magic along the southern village road).
travel_time: ~20–30 minutes walk south-southeast from the Human Village South Gate; ~15 minutes east of Myouren Temple via the scenic loop; ~3 miles (~45 minutes) west-northwest of Misty Lake.
approach_route: Exit the Human Village South Gate (past Suzunaan) and follow the southern road for 20–30 minutes until the open road meets the dense canopy of the Forest of Magic, or take the scenic loop east from Myouren Temple and Kogasa's Forge.
local_customs: Rinnosuke Morichika's neutral curio shop (opens at 09:00); serves as the final landmark where Human Village common sense applies before Forest of Magic territory begins.

short_desc: Damp, spore-choked primeval woodland filled with luminescent mushrooms and eccentric magicians.
long_desc: Stretching south and east from Kourindou toward Misty Lake, the Forest of Magic is an unpatrolled old-growth wilderness where sunlight barely pierces the canopy and hallucinogenic mushroom spores saturate the humid air. Humans shun its miasma, making it an ideal refuge for solitary witches like Marisa Kirisame and Alice Margatroid.
placement_note: 100 meters south of Kourindou at the Fallen-Log Fork inside the damp woodland.
wiki_summary:
The Forest of Magic (魔法の森, Mahou no Mori) is location name in Gensokyo that's a focal point for all things evil, ominous and repulsive, located not far from the Human Village. It's the home to both Marisa Kirisame and Alice Margatroid.

Since Gensokyo isn't a huge place, if you say "forest" (森, Mori), it refers to the Forest of Magic. It's called the "Forest of Magic" because of the wide number of hallucinogenic mushrooms that grow here. Many magicians live in this forest for the sake of increasing their magical powers with these hallucinogenic mushrooms. The forest has areas of ground where the sun never shines, thus making them dark and damp for mushrooms to endlessly grow there. 

It's a place whose true nature is clouded by strange rumours and weird happenstance. The forest's environment is extremely hazardous to both humans and youkai and both kinds typically also find the place uncomfortable. The spores of monstrous mushrooms dance about in mid-air and a normal human's health would worsen simply by breathing here, putting aside the human-eating plants and inevitable, horrible misfortune that will surely befall all who even think of trespassing into the forest. However, if one could stand the noxious gases that the monstrous mushrooms emit, then it would be both a safe and secretive place to seclude oneself, or a fairly nice place to live for people who don't like to be disturbed. 

[Geography & People]
Marisa and Alice's houses are located somewhere within the forest near to each other. Near both their houses is the tree where the Three Fairies of Light used to live, but they have now moved behind the Hakurei Shrine. Rounding out the main attractions is Kourindou, Rinnosuke Morichika's shop of odds and ends (including many objects from the outside world), which is found on the very border of the forest itself.

In Oriental Sacred Place Chapter 10, a radio tower that appeared in the forest from the outside world was converted into a fairy shrine by the Three Fairies of Light.

In Symposium of Post-mysticism, it is known that the forest is one of Mamizou Futatsuiwa's and Shizuha Aki's main places of activity.

travel_time: ~25–30 minutes walk south-southeast from the Human Village South Gate to the northern tree line at Kourindou; the Kourindou Path Fork sits 100 meters (~2 minutes) south inside the forest at a fallen log.
approach_route: Pass Kourindou at the northern forest edge and walk 100 meters south to the Fallen-Log Fork: the left trail loops back toward the village/lake edge, while the right trail (marked by boot prints and broom drag-marks) leads deeper east to Marisa's Cottage and Rumia's Cedar Clearing.
local_customs: Unpatrolled magical wilderness outside village protection; choked with toxic/luminescent mushroom spores, stray spells, and predatory youkai (especially hazardous during the 30-minute dawn overlap).

Inside, brass alembics, drying fungi, and stacks of 'borrowed' grimoires crowd around a central wood stove, while a scorched rear clearing serves for Master Spark testing.

short_desc: Expansive, fog-shrouded alpine lake teeming with ice fairies, mermaids, and giant catfish.
long_desc: Located a 40-minute walk southeast of the Human Village, Misty Lake is fed by mountain streams and perpetually veiled in dense midday fog. Its waters are home to mermaid Wakasagihime and lively fairy courts, while its far eastern shore conceals the Scarlet Devil Mansion.
placement_note: Southeastern basin lake between the Forest of Magic and the Scarlet Devil Mansion.
wiki_summary:
The Misty Lake (霧の湖, Kiri no Mizuumi) is a large lake located at the foot of the Youkai Mountain. Many fairies and youkai alike appear to gather here, especially during the summertime, given the abundant water. The lake and its environs appear to be the home of Cirno, Daiyousei and Wakasagihime.

Commonly, when someone says "The lake" (湖, mizuumi), it usually refers to the Misty Lake. The water in the lake comes from a river originating from the Youkai Mountain. While the Scarlet Devil Mansion was on an island within Misty Lake as of Embodiment of Scarlet Devil, the mansion would be said to be on a bank next to the lake itself rather than on an island in future installments and written works. At and around noon each day, a strange mist envelops the entire lake, making it difficult to see anything (hence the origin of the name). The origin of this mist is unknown, but it appears that because of the bad visibility, the lake isn't as big as one would think – it would take about an hour to walk the full length around the river, so one can estimate the circumference to be about 3.1 miles (5 km).

Extremely large monster fish live in the lake as well, and can occasionally be caught on nights of the new moon. This has led to the lake being popular amongst anglers who aim to catch such a fish. These fish range from 2 to 5 fathoms (in essence up to 9 meters), with the largest on recording as 10 fathoms (this is believed to be an exaggeration).

A Master of the Lake also lives there. However, his house is so deep down that only fish or amphibians may dive down there.

It is said that creatures can't live in the lake, making it way more clear.
atlas_sector: Southeastern Basin Lake (southeast of the Human Village and the Forest of Magic, at the southern foot of Youkai Mountain).
travel_time: ~40 minutes walk southeast from the Human Village across farmland and meadow to the southern rocky shore; ~3 miles across the water to the Scarlet Devil Mansion on the far shore.
approach_route: Exit the Human Village South or East road and follow the southeastern meadow path for ~40 minutes to the rocky southern beach (Cirno's Claim), or walk an additional ~10–15 minutes around the mist-shrouded lakeshore to the Scarlet Devil Mansion gates.
local_customs: Split territory: the southern rocky shore marks the outer limit of Keine's village protection and Cirno's fairy court, while the far shore behind the mist wall is sovereign Scarlet Devil Mansion territory.

short_desc: Rocky southern beach of Misty Lake marking Cirno's fairy court and the outer limit of village protection.
long_desc: At the end of the 40-minute meadow trail from the Human Village stands a prominent lakeside boulder formation claimed by ice fairy Cirno. This rocky shore marks the outermost perimeter of Keine Kamishirasawa's village jurisdiction; stepping past it into the lake mist enters Scarlet Devil Mansion territory.
placement_note: Southern rocky shoreline of Misty Lake directly matching traditional scroll maps.
atlas_sector: Southwestern / Southern Rocky Shoreline of Misty Lake (Cirno's Claim).
travel_time: ~40 minutes walk southeast from the Human Village; ~3 miles across the water (or ~15 minutes shoreline walk) from the Scarlet Devil Mansion.
approach_route: Follow the southeastern meadow trail from the Human Village for 40 minutes until reaching the rocky beach and the large boulder formation of Crawdad Rock.
local_customs: Outer boundary of Keine Kamishirasawa's village protection perimeter and seat of Cirno's shoreline fairy court; stepping past this shore toward the mist wall enters the Scarlet Devil Mansion's forbidden zone.

short_desc: Remilia Scarlet's windowless crimson Gothic manor rising behind the mist wall on Misty Lake's far shore.
long_desc: Transported from Europe and set upon a ridge along Misty Lake's far southeastern shore, the Scarlet Devil Mansion is a towering Gothic clock-tower estate with very few windows. Guarded at the red iron gates by Hong Meiling and governed within by head maid Sakuya Izayoi, its spatial-warped corridors house vampire mistress Remilia Scarlet, her volatile sister Flandre, and mage Patchouli Knowledge.
placement_note: Far southeastern shore of Misty Lake behind the territorial mist wall.
wiki_summary:
The Scarlet Devil Mansion (紅魔館, Koumakan), also referred to as the Scarlet Manor or Scarlet Mansion, is a European-style mansion owned by Remilia Scarlet. While originally located on an island within Misty Lake during Embodiment of Scarlet Devil, it is located on a ridge on the edge of Misty Lake in future installments and written works. From the outside, there are scarlet-colored windows, but there aren't many windows because of the nature of its vampire residents. There are plenty of rooms without windows at all, too. Through the dialogue of Touhou Hisoutensoku and multiple literary works, it can be said that the entrance to the mansion is usually not fully locked. There is a clock tower on the roof, but the bell on it only rings at night.

The inside of the mansion is much larger than is apparent from the outside. This is due to Sakuya Izayoi's ability to manipulate time and space.

The mansion's owner is Remilia Scarlet. Patchouli Knowledge, a friend of hers, resides in the library, while Remilia's sister, Flandre Scarlet, is not allowed to leave the mansion. Hong Meiling acts as the gatekeeper, but is frequently overpowered by many characters. Some time after the events of Ten Desires, a number of hofgoblins were hired on as additional help.

Many fairies are employed by Remilia Scarlet as Fairy Maids in order to clean the mansion, and they're overseen by the head maid, Sakuya Izayoi. The maids don't appear to be very useful, however, since they are just fairies. According to an advertisement in Bohemian Archive in Japanese Red (Cirno's interview), maids are provided with three meals a day and uniforms, but no paid vacations, breaks, or afternoon naps. However, unofficially (in terms of the mansion's policies), the fairy maids are free to do as they please, and another employee gatekeeper Meiling is known to take afternoon "siestas" (which is either close enough to a nap, or an excuse to cover up that it is an actual nap). The advert shows the mansion is open to hiring other beings as maids, and Sakuya has indicated in the vampire team ending in Imperishable Night that if she were to train a successor, it would be human, but currently Sakuya is the only human maid at the mansion. Hieda no Akyuu suggests that there are very rare magic books, and there are also many books from the Outside World. Certainly, unconfirmed to Akyuu, at least some books are in
atlas_sector: Far Southeastern Shore of Misty Lake (~3 miles across the lake from Crawdad Rock, veiled behind territorial mist).
travel_time: ~45–50 minutes walk southeast from the Human Village (~40 minutes to Misty Lake + ~10 minutes around the mist-shrouded lakeshore road to the red iron gates).
approach_route: Walk 40 minutes southeast from the Human Village to Misty Lake -> pass beyond Cirno's southern shore into the territorial mist wall -> approach the Red Iron Front Gates guarded by Hong Meiling and Sakuya Izayoi. (Visible from Hakurei Shrine hill only in autumn when mist thins; the shrine is invisible from the mansion).
local_customs: FORBIDDEN ZONE without formal invitation—Keine's village protection does not extend past Misty Lake's southern shore. Sakuya Izayoi controls all gate entry/exit, shoots down unauthorized flyers, and rearranges non-Euclidean corridors at night.

short_desc: Patchouli Knowledge's subterranean grimoire archive inside the Scarlet Devil Mansion's west wing.
long_desc: Reached down the Scarlet Devil Mansion's ground-floor west corridor past the second arch, Voile is a cavernous underground library containing thousands of elemental grimoires and original spellbooks. Patchouli Knowledge and her assistant Koakuma maintain the silent, warded stacks.
placement_note: West wing / subterranean archive of the Scarlet Devil Mansion.
atlas_sector: Misty Lake Sector (0.81, 0.78)
travel_time: Reachable via regional trails from the nearest hub.
approach_route: West wing / subterranean archive of the Scarlet Devil Mansion.
local_customs: Standard Gensokyo Spell Card & territorial etiquette applies.

name_jp: 紅魔館・客間と大食堂
short_desc: Sun-draped ground-floor reception wing and amber-glass gallery of the Scarlet Devil Mansion.
long_desc: The formal reception wing of the Scarlet Devil Mansion where invited day-guests and evening banquet visitors are received by Remilia Scarlet and Sakuya Izayoi. Heavy velvet drapes seal out daylight, while an adjoining amber-glass conservatory and portrait gallery overlook the mist.
first_appearance: Strange and Bright Nature Deity / Campaign Canon
placement_note: Ground-floor main wing of the Scarlet Devil Mansion.
atlas_sector: Scarlet Devil Mansion Interior — Ground-Floor Reception Wing.
travel_time: ~1–2 minutes walk inside the Scarlet Devil Mansion front entrance hall (~45–50 minutes total walk from the Human Village).
approach_route: Enter through the Scarlet Devil Mansion red iron gates and main foyer under Sakuya's escort into the sun-draped Parlor, Ceremonial Dining Room, amber-glass Portrait Gallery, and adjoining glass Conservatory.
local_customs: Formal day-guest and dinner reception zone governed by Remilia Scarlet's aristocratic etiquette and Sakuya's strict departure schedule; heavy drapes must never be opened during daylight.

name_en: SDM Rose Gardens, East Wing & Basement
name_jp: 紅魔館・庭園と東棟・地下室
short_desc: Meiling's rose gardens, the 2nd-floor lakeside guest suites, and Flandre's restricted deep basement.
long_desc: Surrounding the Scarlet Devil Mansion behind the red iron gates are manicured rose hedges tended by Hong Meiling. Above sit the iron-shuttered second-floor East Wing guest suites and lakeside balconies, while deep beneath the foundations lies the restricted basement of Flandre Scarlet.
placement_note: Outer rose gardens, upper east wing, and lower basement of the Scarlet Devil Mansion.
atlas_sector: Scarlet Devil Mansion Perimeter, Second-Floor East Wing & Restricted Basement.
travel_time: Outer gardens surround the mansion behind the red iron gates (~45 minutes SE of the Human Village); East Wing guest suites sit on the 2nd floor; Flandre's quarters lie in the deep basement.
approach_route: Pass the red iron front gates into the North/East rose gardens patrolled by Meiling, or ascend the interior stairs to the 2nd-floor lakeside balconies and iron-shuttered East Wing guest suites.
local_customs: Overnight guests are restricted to their assigned 2nd-floor East Wing suites after hours; Remilia's sealed private chambers, the Mansion Kitchen, and the Basement stairs to Flandre's quarters are strictly off-limits.

short_desc: Abandoned European-style manor on Misty Lake's northeast shore inhabited by the Prismriver Sisters.
long_desc: Once created by Count Prismriver for his four daughters and later transported into Gensokyo near the northeastern shore of Misty Lake, this melancholic Western mansion echoes day and night with the rehearsals of the poltergeist Prismriver Ensemble.
placement_note: Northeastern shore of Misty Lake at the foot of the Spring Path.
wiki_summary:
The Ruined Western Mansion (, Haiyoukan) is a mansion where the echoes of ensemble rehearsals can be heard, yet none can be seen. It is home to three poltergeists, the Prismriver Sisters.

It was formerly the mansion of Count Prismriver and his four daughters, human aristocrats of the outer world. But, after the family was torn apart by a series of unfortunate events, the mansion was abandoned by all but Layla Prismriver, who refused to leave her beloved home. After Layla conjured poltergeists resembling her three sisters, they and the entire mansion disappeared into Gensokyo by the invocation of an unknown ritual. The mansion is now located in the vicinity of the Misty Lake.

Although the ghostly echoes may be disturbing to the mentally unprepared, any visitor can attempt to enlist the Prismriver Sisters for a musical performance. They are often seen around Gensokyo and the Netherworld at various events to generate publicity.
atlas_sector: Misty Lake Sector (0.73, 0.71)
travel_time: Reachable via regional trails from the nearest hub.
approach_route: Northeastern shore of Misty Lake at the foot of the Spring Path.
local_customs: Standard Gensokyo Spell Card & territorial etiquette applies.

name_jp: 春雪異変の道・春の小径
short_desc: Cherry-blossom-lined mountain trail northeast of Misty Lake rising toward the Barrier of Life and Death.
long_desc: Climbing from the northeastern shore of Misty Lake past the Ruined Western Mansion toward the cloud line, the Spring Path bursts with seasonal blossoms and noisy fairies whenever Lily White announces spring. Its upper skyward terminus leads to the Barrier of Life and Death.
placement_note: Lakeshore-to-ridge trail northeast of Misty Lake.
wiki_summary:
The Spring Path (春の小径, Haru no Komichi) is a long path full of flowers and cherry blossom.

There isn't much information about the path as a whole. It seems to be connected to the Misty Lake and the Forest of Magic. The ground is overwhelmed with flowers and it is plausible that it is covered with cherry blossoms. The name may be derived from the falling cherry petals and blooming flowers which is an occurring event during spring. It is also possibly related to Reimu's theme "Spring Lane ~ Colorful Path" from Phantasmagoria of Flower View.
atlas_sector: Eastern / Northeastern Lakeshore Trail near Misty Lake rising toward the Barrier of Life and Death.
travel_time: ~45–55 minutes walk east-southeast from the Human Village (just past the northern/eastern shore of Misty Lake).
approach_route: Walk to Misty Lake's northern/eastern shore past the Ruined Western Mansion and follow the cherry-blossom-lined path ascending toward the sky boundary.
local_customs: Fairy-crowded seasonal flower trail leading toward the Netherworld's colossal sky gate.

short_desc: Vast, shifting labyrinth of towering green bamboo 40 minutes east of the Human Village.
long_desc: Reached by walking 40 minutes east across the terraced rice paddies from the Human Village East Gate, the Bamboo Forest of the Lost disorients intruders with rapidly growing stalks, uniform scenery, and Eientei's spatial boundary spells. Immortal guide Fujiwara no Mokou escorts lost humans and patients through its mist-shrouded trails.
placement_note: Eastern basin maze across the terraced paddies from the Human Village East Gate.
wiki_summary:
The Bamboo Forest of the Lost (迷いの竹林, Mayoi no Chikurin) is said to be located in the opposite direction to the Youkai Mountain when looking out from the Human Village. Legend has it that the forest was not originally a part of Gensokyo, but was washed over to Gensokyo by a big tsunami. Long long ago, the forest was known as Takakusa Commandery (高草郡, Takakusa Gun). Inside of it lies the mansion Eientei.

Given the nature of the forest, it is very easy to get lost. There are no clearings, the ground is mostly flat & indistinguishable and the bamboos grow quickly resulting in a constant change of scenery.

Fujiwara no Mokou lives here assisting any people who get lost, while Tewi Inaba and other rabbits can be seen wandering in the forest.
atlas_sector: Eastern / Southeastern Basin Maze (across the terraced rice paddies east-southeast of the Human Village).
travel_time: ~40 minutes walk east-southeast from the Human Village East Gate to the bamboo perimeter; interior traversal takes ~10–15 minutes with a guide.
approach_route: Exit the Human Village East Palisade Gate -> follow the southeast road across terraced farmland and rice paddies for 40 minutes -> meet Fujiwara no Mokou at the slanted, mist-shrouded bamboo edge.
local_customs: Outside Human Village protection; bamboo paths shift layout between walks, and Eientei's earth rabbits patrol the interior trails and report movement to Eirin.

short_desc: Exiled Lunarian palace and medical clinic hidden deep inside the Bamboo Forest of the Lost.
long_desc: Concealed for over a millennium behind a spell of eternity inside the Bamboo Forest, Eientei is a grand Heian-style wooden estate inhabited by Princess Kaguya Houraisan and sage Eirin Yagokoro. While the main courtyard remains guarded by Reisen and Tewi's earth rabbits, Eirin operates Gensokyo's premier apothecary and medical clinic through the east entrance.
placement_note: Deep eastern sector inside the Bamboo Forest of the Lost.
wiki_summary:
Eientei (永遠亭, lit. "House of Eternity") is the name of a large, old-fashioned Japanese mansion hidden deep within the Bamboo Forest of the Lost. It has hallways that lead out into the far reaches of the sky. It was created by Eirin Yagokoro for Kaguya Houraisan.

Eientei is currently occupied by a large group. Kaguya Houraisan and Eirin Yagokoro have been hiding there since their exile from the Moon. Other occupants include rabbits, lots of them, all under the command of Tewi Inaba, who protect Kaguya and Eirin from intruders.

It is unknown to the majority of Gensokyo that the residents of Eientei are from the moon. Eientei's residents and the few nonresidents who do know are keeping it a secret. Youkai are apparently aware that Reisen is from the Moon (who proclaims it), but the humans from the Human Village may not be. The average human and youkai know Kaguya as the princess of Eientei and its mistress.

Every month on the night of the full moon, the residents of Eientei hold a Moon Festival (例月祭, Reigetsusai), offering mochi with medicinal herbs pounded into them. Making mochi is thus the main occupation of the Earth rabbits. Eientei has also hosted a lunar expo at least twice, showcasing objects from the Moon. Items include the American flag placed on the moon (confiscated from the Three Fairies of Light), moon rocks, an ox cart used to be able to fly long ago (but now is pulled by an actual ox), a kimono that shines, a lunar rover and many other relics.

Both humans and youkai may come to Eientei for Eirin's medical services. Fujiwara no Mokou often provides escort through the Bamboo Forest of the Lost. In Alternative Facts in Eastern Utopia, Eientei group's service providing medicines is called "Hourai Pharmacy".
atlas_sector: Deep Eastern Sector inside the Bamboo Forest of the Lost (hidden Lunarian compound and medical clinic).
travel_time: ~45–55 minutes total walk east-southeast from the Human Village East Gate (~40 min across farmland to the Bamboo Forest edge + ~10–15 min guided walk through shifting bamboo trails).
approach_route: Walk 40 minutes east-southeast from the Human Village East Gate into the Bamboo Forest of the Lost -> follow Mokou's escort or rabbit trail markers -> approach via the East-Entrance Medical Clinic door rather than the main courtyard.
local_customs: Sovereign household of Kaguya Houraisan and Eirin Yagokoro outside village authority; visitors must state their name at the east-entrance clinic and wait for rabbit escort.

short_desc: Fujiwara no Mokou's solitary thatched dwelling and yakitori stand near the Bamboo Forest perimeter.
long_desc: Situated along a hidden bamboo clearing near the western approach from the Human Village, this modest thatched hut is the home of Hourai immortal Fujiwara no Mokou. Keine Kamishirasawa frequently visits here on Thursdays and full-moon nights.
first_appearance: Cage in Lunatic Runagate / Wild and Horned Hermit
placement_note: Western perimeter of the Bamboo Forest of the Lost along the village approach road.
atlas_sector: Bamboo Forest Sector (0.72, 0.38)
travel_time: Reachable via regional trails from the nearest hub.
approach_route: Western perimeter of the Bamboo Forest of the Lost along the village approach road.
local_customs: Standard Gensokyo Spell Card & territorial etiquette applies.

short_desc: Isolated, lily-of-the-valley-carpeted hillside inhabited by doll youkai Medicine Melancholy.
long_desc: Rising on the remote flank overlooking the Bamboo Forest of the Lost, Nameless Hill is carpeted in blooming lilies-of-the-valley whose concentrated pollen saturates the air with slow-acting poison. Abandoned dolls used to be discarded here, giving birth to the sentient doll youkai Medicine Melancholy.
placement_note: Remote eastern ridge beyond the Bamboo Forest of the Lost.
wiki_summary:
The Hill of the Nameless (無名の丘, Mumei no Oka) is a meadow full of purple and white lilies-of-the-valley on a mountain opposite Youkai Mountain. In the past, it was used as a place to abandon children who then later either died from the poison of the lilies or were abducted by youkai. It is somehow hidden away from the Human Village.

Not much is known about the location. The "Nameless" (無名) part is derived from the nameless children who were abandoned at the hill to be killed by the flowers there, only to be collected later by youkai. However, there are legends that some of the children were abducted and raised by mischievous youkai. Stories have been told that parents who did not want to see their own children die left them here in the hope that they can live with the youkai. It's believed that, because of these stories, people don't come here, not even youkai. It is believed to be the place where Medicine Melancholy came into being. The threat level of this place is 'Medium' and fairies and phantoms can typically be encountered here. The place seems to not get much direct sunlight and is fairly windy, so this place may not be warm at times.
atlas_sector: Remote Southern / Opposite Flank of Youkai Mountain overlooking the Bamboo Forest.
travel_time: ~75–90 minutes walk from the Human Village across the eastern hills beyond the Bamboo Forest.
approach_route: Cross past the Bamboo Forest of the Lost or climb the opposite low ridge of Youkai Mountain into the fields of wild lilies-of-the-valley.
local_customs: Isolated, poison-carpeted hillside inhabited by Medicine Melancholy where abandoned dolls and dense lily-of-the-valley toxins endanger humans.

short_desc: Endless golden basin of head-high sunflowers tended by ancient flower youkai Yuuka Kazami.
long_desc: Hidden deep inland beyond the Bamboo Forest trails, the Garden of the Sun is a sunlit bowl carpeted with millions of towering sunflowers that bloom brightly through summer. Fairies flock here by day and the Prismriver Ensemble occasionally holds outdoor concerts, but anyone who tramples a single stem faces Yuuka Kazami's wrath.
placement_note: Sunlit inland flower basin south of the Bamboo Forest of the Lost.
wiki_summary:
The Garden of the Sun (太陽の畑, Taiyō no Hata) is a field full of sunflowers that is home to numerous fairies and youkai, including Yuuka Kazami and Eternity Larva.

The threat level to this location is 'medium' and fairies are easily encounterable. The garden is filled with dazzling yellow sunflowers, and it is said that it is located in the heart of Gensokyo, from the opposite side of a mountain. It's apparently shaped a bit like a south-facing bowl, so it's hard to find it from a distance. It is also located not far from the Human Village, where some humans may come here to look at its beauty. However, this field can become a concert venue for spirited youkai during the night. If a human carelessly got caught in one, you'll likely be surrounded by a great number of youkai; however, it might not be a big issue, but escaping would be difficult. The Prismriver Sisters often perform here.

The sunflowers seem quite ordinary, so the field is a popular sunbathing spot for fairies in the day. Even if humans came during the day, they'd be mocked by a great number of fairies. Therefore, Hieda no Akyuu says she hides somewhere whilst viewing the field.

Yuuka Kazami can be found here due to the number of sunflowers, having it her most active area. An anonymous person stated that they saw her here with a terrifying smile, making them run away. However, it's unknown if she actually lives here. In the PC-98 canon, she lives in Mugenkan within the Fantasy World, located behind the Hakurei Shrine.
atlas_sector: Hidden Interior Heartland of Gensokyo (vast sunflower basin surrounding Mugenkan).
travel_time: ~60–75 minutes walk from the Human Village through unmapped meadow trails.
approach_route: Follow the hidden inland flower trails deep into Gensokyo's interior until the terrain opens into endless fields of head-high sunflowers.
local_customs: Yuuka Kazami's personal territory; fairies and Prismriver concerts gather here peacefully, but anyone damaging the sunflowers or refusing to leave faces Yuuka's overwhelming force.

short_desc: Yuuka Kazami's secluded mansion at the heart of the Garden of the Sun and border of the Fantasy World.
long_desc: Resting at the center of the labyrinthine sunflower sea of the Garden of the Sun (and historically anchored to the Lake of Blood border), Mugenkan is the private Western-style manor of Yuuka Kazami, guarded at its threshold by the scythe-wielding gatekeeper Elly.
placement_note: Heart of the Garden of the Sun.
wiki_summary:
Mugenkan (夢幻館, Mugenkan) is a mysterious mansion located within the Lake of Blood. It is the final destination for the player in Lotus Land Story.

[Geography]
The mansion itself apparently lies on the boundary between Gensokyo and the Fantasy World. Physically, this boundary is located beneath the Lake of Blood somehow, which is in the middle of a lake on a mountain behind the Hakurei Shrine.

According to Lotus Land story's manual, the fifth stage of the game is set in the innermost part of Mugenkan. The background is shown to be largely pitch black, with big blue stars scrolling by and slightly illuminating it.

[People]
Yuuka Kazami appears to be the sole occupant of the mansion, though Elly does guard the entrance, and Kurumi guards the lake on top of it.

[Appearance]
At the end of the third stage of Lotus Land Story, there are lots of blue tiles on the ground in front of the door of Mugenkan, and the gatekeeper of the entrance Elly throws some of those tiles at the beginning of the boss battle.

On the fourth stage, there red checkerboard pattern floor that continues down a corridor, and somewhere in the middle of the stage, there are two six-starred magic circles.

On fifth stage, there are three floating blue checkerboard platforms, and below there are big blue transparent stars that moves down the screen constantly. Also below the stars, there appears to be a number of watches.
atlas_sector: Center of the Garden of the Sun (and border nexus with the Lake of Blood).
travel_time: ~75 minutes walk from the Human Village to the heart of the Garden of the Sun.
approach_route: Cross the labyrinthine sunflower fields of the Garden of the Sun (or pass Elly's scythe gate at the Lake of Blood) to reach the western-style mansion.
local_customs: Private residence of Yuuka Kazami guarded by Elly; uninvited entry is suicidal.

short_desc: Crimson mountain-border lake guarded by vampire girl Kurumi at the old threshold to Mugenkan.
long_desc: A high, eerie basin filled with blood-red water situated along the old dimensional border behind Mugenkan. Vampire girl Kurumi keeps vigil along its crimson shore to deter uninvited intruders from crossing toward Yuuka's domain.
placement_note: Border basin adjacent to Mugenkan.
wiki_summary:
The Lake of Blood is a lake in the mountains that appears to be filled with pure blood, rather than water. It appears in the second stage of Lotus Land Story. Within it lies the entrance to Mugenkan.

Kurumi is the gatekeeper of the entrance to the lake. Elly stands guard within the lake, at the border between Gensokyo and the Fantasy World, protecting the entrance to Mugenkan. On stage 2 of Lotus Land Story, a whole lake appears to be made of blood. It even has rocks in it. After Kurumi made her appearance as the midboss of that stage, the background then appears to be black and several rocks wrapped in shimenawa ropes have lined up. The manual states that stage 3 is within the lake after its water has drained out.
atlas_sector: High Mountain Border Basin (crimson lake marking the old threshold to Mugenkan).
travel_time: ~90 minutes climb into the mountain crags from the Human Village.
approach_route: Ascend the isolated mountain crag trail past Kurumi's shoreline vigil to the blood-red lake where Elly guards the boundary to Mugenkan.
local_customs: Guarded by Kurumi and Elly; hostile to uninvited intruders.

short_desc: Spirit-hidden mountain village and residence of Yukari Yakumo, Ran Yakumo, and Chen.
long_desc: An illusory abandoned village and grand traditional mansion hidden deep in the mountain border woods. Because Yukari Yakumo's boundary manipulation conceals its existence, travelers cannot reach Mayohiga by deliberate navigation—only those spirited in or invited find the mist parting before its gates.
placement_note: Eastern mountain border woods near the Great Hakurei Barrier.
wiki_summary:
Mayohiga (マヨヒガ or 迷ひ家) is a lost village somewhere around the Great Hakurei Barrier. It is abandoned by humans, but is home to many cats that Chen has brought there.

"In an abandoned estate in the mountain recesses, in which a lost traveler, upon taking and returning with some daily necessities, received good luck," so to speak appeared as such in the Touhou Project. Like the Hakurei Shrine, it is located deep within the mountains near the Great Hakurei Barrier. It is unclear whether "mountain" refers to the Youkai Mountain or to some other. However, while the shrine is physically on both sides of the barrier, Mayohiga acts as the rest of the barrier separating Gensokyo from the Outside World. Humans who come near the barrier will start to become disoriented and lost, and if they continue onwards, they will find themselves spirited away to the almost dreamlike village of Mayohiga.

The Village of Cats (猫の棲む里, Neko no Sumu Sato) is believed to be located in Mayohiga, far away from the Human Village, where it is a place that Chen tries to make the cats here her servants, but fails to do so, as the cats do not obey her orders and live by their own on a chaotic state. Chen brought the cats here because humans abandoned this village ages ago. 

It is a very likely that the explanation of Yukari Yakumo and Ran Yakumo living in Mayohiga is actually not true. Yukari's residence has been described as "A place of unknown location that no-one should ever be able to reach," but Mayohiga is occasionally stumbled upon by lost humans, from which it is also possible to return safely. Moreover, the presence of information on Mayohiga in the Gensokyo Chronicle show some awareness of its existence on the humans' part.
[Name]
The spellings マヨヒガ, 迷ひ家, and Mayohiga are all archaisms based on the pre-WWII orthography and do not reflect the pronunciation of the name. Modernly, it is spelled マヨイガ in katakana, 迷い家 in kanamajiri, and Mayoiga in Romaji. In Perfect Cherry Blossom, the old katakana spelling is used in the stage title while the modern kanamajiri spelling is used in the dialogue.

[Folkloric Basis]
The original source of Mayohiga appears to be from 1910 book , a collection of folk stories by Kunio Yanagita, known to be the founding father of Japanese folklore. The tale, told mainly in the northeast of Japan, is about a strange house reached by people wandering into anothe
atlas_sector: Shifting Spirit-Hidden Village near the Great Hakurei Barrier and mountain woods.
travel_time: Variable (~45–60 minutes walk into the border mountain woods, but reachable only when Yukari or Ran permits the mist boundary to part).
approach_route: Wander the deep mountain woods near the Great Hakurei Barrier until the phantom village manifests through the mist.
local_customs: Home of Yukari Yakumo, Ran Yakumo, and Chen; impossible to locate by normal navigation unless invited or spirited in.

short_desc: Hexagonal basalt river gorge at the northern base of Youkai Mountain where Kappa and Yamawaro trade.
long_desc: Located a 45–60 minute walk north from the Human Village North Gate, Genbu Ravine is a dramatic canyon of columnar basalt cliffs carved by the runoff from Wind God's Lake. Kappa engineers like Nitori Kawashiro and yamawaro merchants like Takane Yamashiro contest water rights and run workshops along its banks.
first_appearance: TH10 / Wild and Horned Hermit / image4.png
placement_note: Northern foothills gorge directly north of the Human Village North Gate, matching traditional scroll maps.
wiki_summary:
stub

Genbu Ravine (玄武の沢, Genbu no Sawa) is a ravine named after the legendary tortoise Genbu (). Formed when Youkai Mountain was still an active volcano. The bottom is covered with hexagonal cracks so it looks like a turtle shell, and it is surrounded by six-sided cliffs. This bizarre rock formation was made when lava flowing from Youkai Mountain cooled and hardened. According to Symposium of Post-mysticism, it is home to some of the kappa, including Nitori Kawashiro. Recently, pipes have been shown to be running though the walls of the ravine.
atlas_sector: Northern Foothills Gorge at the base of Youkai Mountain (Kappa and Yamawaro industrial waterway).
travel_time: ~45–60 minutes walk north from the Human Village North Gate.
approach_route: Exit the Human Village North Gate and follow the river valley upstream into the northern foothills until reaching the hexagonal basalt cliffs and waterfall basin.
local_customs: Industrial river gorge outside village protection where Kappa (Nitori's engineering workshops) and Yamawaro (Takane) operate and compete.

short_desc: Secluded rocky valley floor just upstream of Genbu Ravine hosting the primary Kappa bazaar.
long_desc: Ten minutes upstream from the lower entrance of Genbu Ravine at the very foot of Youkai Mountain, Untrodden Valley shelters the main Kappa engineering workshops and seasonal flea markets. Outsiders require kappa trade business or Nitori's vouching to browse safely.
placement_note: Immediately upstream north-northeast of Genbu Ravine at the base of Youkai Mountain.
wiki_summary: The Untrodden Valley (未踏の渓谷, Mitou no Keikoku) is a valley located at the very base of the Youkai Mountain through which a river running from the Waterfall of Nine Heavens courses. The kappa's hideout, the home of the kappa as mentioned in Wild and Horned Hermit, lies somewhere on land in this area.
atlas_sector: Northern Foothills Ravine at the very base of Youkai Mountain (adjacent to Genbu Ravine).
travel_time: ~50–65 minutes walk north from the Human Village North Gate (~10 minutes past the lower entrance of Genbu Ravine).
approach_route: Follow the northern river gorge upstream from the Human Village North Gate past Genbu Ravine's basalt cliffs into the hidden valley floor.

The Giant Toad's Pond (大蝦蟇の池, Oo-gama no Ike) is a small, mysterious pond that can be found halfway up the Youkai Mountain.

It is rather difficult to get to this place due to being in the middle of the mountain. The pond's water is said to have divine properties necessary for Shinto rituals, and lotus flowers can be seen growing on its surface. The lotus flowers in the pond are beautiful and lotus leaves and flowers floating on the surface lit by sunbeams filtered through the surrounding foliage further emphasize the mysteriousness of the pond. There is a small shrine located near to the pond about which not much is known. It was built so long ago that no one knows who it was built by or for whom any more. Humans sometimes leave offerings here. The offering left here immediately disappear, believed to be taken by the tengu.

The threat level of this place is 'medium', and it is home to the Giant Toad, the protector of the pond. It is said to violently attack those who desecrate the pond, but be otherwise passive. It is said that he protects those who leave it offerings, and that a sign of its protection is to be trailed by toads. This is also the location where Cirno was eaten by the Giant Toad.

Youkai Mountain (妖怪の山, Youkai no Yama) is Gensokyo's largest mountain and volcano. As its name implies, it is inhabited almost exclusively by youkai, primarily kappa and tengu, and where humans are generally not welcome.

Initially described in Perfect Memento in Strict Sense, it later became a key location in Mountain of Faith when the Moriya Shrine was transported near to the mountain's summit.

.The Youkai Mountain is a rocky landform covered by a large expanse of forest named The Great Youkai Forest at its foot, with waterfalls and rivers flowing from the lakes at the mountain top. It is known to have been a highly active volcano in the past, but it has been a long time since it last erupted. Smoke is still seen rising from the mountain from time to time. Commonly, when someone says "The mountain" (山, yama), it usually refers to the Youkai Mountain.

It has served as the home of youkai since long before the time of man and is a high threat to humans. Consisting of a close-knit societies of kappa and tengu, the mountain is closed off from outsiders and its inhabitants lead peaceful communal lives. Recently, the mountain has become more open to humans with the construction of the Moriya Ropeway, which allows passengers to travel to the Moriya Shrine and back without passing through tengu lands.

There are rumours stating that there exists a large hollow cavity within the mountain, where a futuristic utopia just like the Outside World is being built, but the tengu's newspapers may not be telling the truth. The sun's light shines all day long there, and an automated factory produces the necessary items to meet the needs of everyday life, and the youkai drink sake while reading the newspaper and discussing the news, living blissfully. Within this hollow cavity, the forbidden act of opening a hole that connects to the outside world through the boundary is perpetrated, so other humans and youkai are not allowed to enter.

The Komakusa Gambling Den (駒草の賭場) is a casino owned by Sannyo Komakusa.

The gambling den is located on Youkai Mountain cliffs such as the False Heaven Shelf, and it only opens on specific days. The den constantly rotates locations among the various abandoned buildings found there, with its current location being signified by a dragon pipe hanging in front of it. In addition to the hanging pipe, it is also represented by a stylized logo of a Komakusa. This logo is present on chips, small sections for distributing dice and games, even some of Sannyo's clothing, and is later used in addition to the pipe, on the sign used to show when Geidontei is rented out as Komakusa Gambling House. Regular patrons of the den are mountain youkai such as kappa, tengu, and yamawaro.

Sannyo constantly fills the place with smoke produced by 100-percent natural Youkai Mountain tobacco, in order to influence to behavior of its guests and prevent the kinds of frenzies that tend to break out in other gambling dens. It's because of this smoke that the den is considered a fine and gentlemanly recreational spot. 
The den is filled with candles, tables, and mats. There is a dragon depicted on the inner side of the entrance door. It has various potted flower arrangements scattered throughout, and [https://tokutenlove.livedoor.blog/archives/24929278.html in a sectioned off room there is a large dragon divider with more flower arrangements] .
When the den's current location is done being used, it is completely emptied

wiki_summary:
The Moriya Shrine (守矢神社, Moriya Jinja) is a Shinto shrine, originally from the Outside World, that was transported to Gensokyo by the god Kanako Yasaka during the start of the events of Mountain of Faith. It is now located somewhere near the top of Youkai Mountain beside the neighboring Wind God's Lake that was brought with it.

This shrine is home to the Shrine Maiden Sanae Kochiya and its resident gods Kanako Yasaka and Suwako Moriya. Both the kappa and tengu have come to accept Kanako as a resident god and now live in peace. As the shrine got few visitors, its primary source of income came from selling bits of outside-world technology to the kappa. Since then, completion of the tramway has made the shrine more accessible and may have also made it more popular among Human Village residents.

As noted in Silent Sinner in Blue, a distinctively thick shimenawa is hung across the entrance of the shrine building, bigger than the one at the Hakurei Shrine. Moriya Shrine has a tiny branch shrine on the grounds of the Hakurei Shrine, and a number of roadside shrines around the outskirts of the Human Village. After years of negotiation with the tengu, an aerial tramway was opened in the spring of 2017, directly connecting the shrine to the foot of the mountain and making it accessible to even normal humans. Sanae Kochiya mentions the shrine having a sacred tree in Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost.

In chapter 19 of Silent Sinner in Blue, Yukari Yakumo talks to Watatsuki no Toyohime and accuses the Lunarians of placing the two thick shimenawa at the front of the Moriya Shrine to seal in the war god, Take-Minakata, because they feared his retribution after conquering his father Daikoku's lands. According to Shinto legend, Amaterasu (generally implied in the Touhou Project to be sister of Lord Tsukuyomi, founder of the Lunar Capital) sent Take-Mikazuchi to conquer Take-Minakata while trying to unite Japan. After a sumo match, Take-minakata's arms were cut and he fled to Lake Suwa, where he married a Suwa goddess, Yasakatome. The conversation is interrupted before Yukari's claim can be confirmed. However, the fact that Toyohime decided to leave Yukari behind on Earth as opposed to taking Yukari prisoner to the Moon like she initially planned to do could imply there is some truth to Yukari's claim.

The Wind God's Lake (風神の湖, Fuujin no Mizuumi), also called the Youkai Mountain Lake (妖怪の山の湖, Yōkai no Yama no Mizūmi) or the Yasaka Lake (八坂の湖, Yasaka no Mizūmi), is a great lake located at the heights of the Youkai Mountain. It was transported into Gensokyo by Kanako Yasaka before the events of Mountain of Faith along with the Moriya Shrine, which is also located nearby. The lake is named after Kanako who, although revered as a goddess of mountains, is in fact a goddess of wind and rain.

Large pillars known as Onbashira (御柱) surround the lake's perimeter, and these are decorated with shimenawa and shide. As of Legacy of Lunatic Kingdom, these aren't shown. Onbashira, literally meaning "honored pillars", are part of a festival held at Suwa Grand Shrine named the Onbashira Festival (御柱祭, Onbashira matsuri). It is held every six years at the shrine, and involves the replacement of previous wooden pillars with newly chopped ones.

As with the Moriya Shrine and the Suwa Grand Shrine, the Wind God's Lake is based on and perhaps intended to be Lake Suwa, although unlike the former there is nothing in its name to suggest a correlation besides the proximity between the lake and the Moriya Shrine.

The Shining Needle Castle (輝針城, Kishinjou) is a castle that's located in the sky near the base of Youkai Mountain. It's also referred to as the Inverted Castle (逆さ城, Sakasajou), though it's unknown whether this is a proper name for the castle or just an informal description of it. It is the home of Shinmyoumaru Sukuna.

According to Shinmyoumaru's profile, the castle was created with the power of the Miracle Mallet by Issun-Boushi's descendants, and, as the power of the Mallet ran out due to it being overused, the castle got reversed.

There are some possible inspirations to the castle, which are:
*There is a stage [http://castlevania.wikia.com/wiki/Castlevania:_Symphony_of_the_Night#The_Inverted_Castle "Inverted Castle"] (逆さ城, Sakasajou) in Castlevania: Symphony of the Night.
*Some people think that Inverted Castle is also inspired by "Treasure Palace of Stone" (石の宝殿, Ishi no Houden), "Rock House of Stability" (鎮の石室, Shizu no iwaya) or commonly known as Floating Stone (浮石, Ukiishi), which is located at Oushiko Shrine in Hyougo Prefecture.

It has some different legends. According to the official booklet of its history, Ōkuninushi and SukunaBikona arrived there from their original land Izumo in order to found the lands, and worked together to construct the stone palace just one night. This facility was planned for the stability and peace of living and governing. In the middle of working, the rebellion of Aga gods occurred, which forced the two to interrupt their action, to gather gods for their side, and to flatten the enemy. Next morning, the rebellion was pacified but the stone palace was unfinished; the two didn't leave it away cruelly, but enspirited it and promised that they keep the land stable.

On the other hand, there is another legend as an oral legend: Some god came to the mind that everyone must be surprised to see the treasurous palace made of rock, then he commanded its construction to other gods. Amanojaku was one of them. His part was the disposal of stones cut off. He wanted to stop the work, then mimic the cock-a-doodle-doo of rooster. The gods working around him mistook it for the opening of the day. At last, they concluded that they weren't able to finish the construction, and went home to let it overturned.

Asama Purifying Mountain (浅間浄穢山, Asama-jouesan) is a man-made, pyramid-shaped mountain located beneath the Sanctuary at the foothills of Youkai Mountain and first appeared in Fossilized Wonders. 

The pyramid was originally a temple to a shrine dedicated to Ariya Iwanaga and Yuiman Asama, named and modeled after the real-world Mount Asama, with the Sanctuary as its courtyard and the petrified forest below the pyramid being the original shrine grounds. Reimu Hakurei initially theorizes that Asama Purifying Mountain used to be Mount Minakami that eventually transported into Gensokyo after Sumireko Usami informs her an old legend of the mountain from the outside world. Ubame Chirizuka, after saying it would be different due to already having a natural mountain there, then theorizes that the Asama Purifying Mountain took the form of a pyramid due to old legends of Mount Minakami from the outside world influencing Asuma Mountain due to it being built on top the petrified forest and shrine instead, which Reimu then considers to be the truth.

It was eventually taken control of by the Lunarians and transformed into a facility to filter out "impurity" (human life information) to preserve the eternal longevity of the Lunar Capital. In doing so, the Lunarians sealed Ariya inside the shrine and brainwashed Yuiman into using her ability to process impurities flowing in from the Outside World. In order to keep the two of them under control, the Lunarians then buried the pyramid underground, and allowed the land placed on top of the pyramid to grow over, becoming the modern-day Sanctuary.
