long_desc: Hovering in the stratosphere directly above Youkai Mountain and Moriya Shrine, Heaven (Bhava-agra) is a realm of floating stone islands, immortal peach orchards, and carefree banquets inhabited by Celestials like Tenshi Hinanawi and dragon-cloud messenger Iku Nagae.
placement_note: Directly above the summit of Youkai Mountain in the upper sky layer.
wiki_summary:
Heaven (天界, Tenkai) is a collection of separate realms existing above the Earth. One of them, Bhavaagra (有頂天, Uchouten), is the setting of most final battles in Scarlet Weather Rhapsody, and can be reached by climbing the Youkai Mountain. Bhavaagra is also where Tenshi Hinanawi and her family live. Suika Ibuki may occasionally be seen there as well.

Those who have achieved nirvana in the cycle of reincarnation or are judged worthy by the Yama may ascend to Heaven. In recent times, access via nirvana has been put on hold, with the official statement from Heaven being that the realm has become overcrowded and can no longer hold any more people. However, Yukari Yakumo has stated that this a lie, and that there is still plenty of free space in Heaven.

Celestials, Angels, and other heavenly beings reside there. These residents generally live carefree lives filled with fishing, song, dance, sake, and peaches. They may also find enjoyment in viewing events that unfold on the Earth.

[History]
It's claimed by Eirin Yagokoro that long ago, Heaven itself was a giant keystone on Earth. When the keystone was pulled out, the planet was devastated and all life on it perished as a consequence. This event occurred so long ago that even some of the oldest known beings such as Eirin had not yet been born.

[Terminology]
In Buddhist terminology, "Bhavaagra" has pretty much the same meaning as "Sphere of Neither Perception nor Non-perception". The characters is a translation from Sanskrit of "Bhavaagra" (), and literally means "summit of the existent world." (Furthermore, the transliteration of Sanskrit generally does not use hyphens, so "Bhava-agra" is not quite correct even though it is used often, and "Bhavāgra" is not accurate either.) Furthermore, since it is a summary saying "the highest", this word is frequently colloquially used to mean "to reach the summit and forget the self, riding with the flow" (Japanese-English dictionaries commonly list this as "ecstasy").

According to the cosmology of Buddhism, in the worlds known as the "three realms", the highest is the "formless realm", and even higher is the territory called the "sphere of neither perception nor non-perception". The three realms, in the order of abandoning desire, are split into the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm.

travel_time: ~3 to 4 hours climb/flight from the Human Village (above Moriya Shrine and Wind God's Lake at the peak of Youkai Mountain).
approach_route: Ascend past the summit of Youkai Mountain and Moriya Shrine through the dragon-cloud layer into the peach-orchard islands of the Celestials.
local_customs: Domain of the Hinanawi clan (Tenshi Hinanawi) and oarfish messenger Iku Nagae; uninvited mortals who have not attained nirvana are treated as trespassers.

short_desc: Bustling twilight market road behind Youkai Mountain leading souls toward the Sanzu River.
long_desc: Skirting the northern rear slope of Youkai Mountain toward the Sanzu River dock, the Road of Liminality is a surprisingly lively lantern-lit market street where ghosts, youkai, and humans run festival stalls for departing spirits.
placement_note: Rear northern slope of Youkai Mountain linking the mountain back-side to the Sanzu River.
wiki_summary:
The Road of Liminality (中有の道, Chūu no Michi) is a road in the back of the Youkai Mountain that leads to the Sanzu River. Though mainly traversed by ghosts and phantoms, the living can also walk down this road.

The threat level here is "low". Even it is full of phantoms and ghosts, the place is very active due to its stands. As Hell was beginning to become difficult to sustain on solely the fees levied on departed souls crossing the Sanzu River, numerous merchant's stands were set up as attractions. Because of this, the road is as lively as a shrine festival, and offers things such as "soul candy" and chances to catch dead goldfish. The stands, however, are run by criminals that were already sentenced to Hell, so oftentimes people passing through will fall for their dirty tricks. If the merchants get caught conning customers, they are sent back to Hell.

Apparently, the festivities sometimes cause the spirit of a dead person to remember the happy times of their life, and retrace their steps to return to life. Even people who life festivals will come here.
atlas_sector: Rear (Northern) Slope of Youkai Mountain connecting the mountain back-side to the Sanzu River.
travel_time: ~120–140 minutes walk north around the rear flank of Youkai Mountain from the Human Village.
approach_route: Skirt the back of Youkai Mountain along the mist-shrouded path lined with twilight stalls run by humans, youkai, and harmless wandering spirits.
local_customs: Liminal boundary market road between the living mountain and the afterlife border; relatively calm, though walking too far north leads straight to the Sanzu River.

short_desc: Fog-bound boundary river between the living world and the afterlife, ferried by Komachi Onozuka.
long_desc: Separating Gensokyo from Higan beyond the Road of Liminality and Sai no Kawara's stone-stacking bank, the Sanzu River flows through permanent mist. Nothing can float or swim in its waters except the boats of shinigami like Komachi Onozuka, while Urumi Ushizaki raises extinct giant fish along the shore.
placement_note: Northwest afterlife boundary river between the Road of Liminality and Higan.
wiki_summary:
The Sanzu River (三途の河, Sanzu no Kawa) is the mist-shrouded river that dead souls must cross in order to reach Higan, where they will await judgment. Part of the riverbank is accessible from Gensokyo, even though the river's source, mouth and opposite bank lie outside it. Only the dead can cross the river on a shinigami's boat if they can afford to pay; everything except shinigami and their boats will sink. The river is populated by the phantoms of extinct marine life, including those from prehistoric times.

Komachi Onozuka may be seen ferrying souls here when she isn't slacking off. In Japanese Buddhist tradition, the Sanzu is said to have three crossings which vary in perilousness depending on the amount of sin a soul committed during his or her lifetime (hence the name). However, this concept is not used in Touhou: instead, Komachi uses her power of distance manipulation to vary the width of the river according to the souls' sinfulness.
atlas_sector: Afterlife Boundary River beyond the Road of Liminality and Muenzuka.
travel_time: ~130–150 minutes walk to the ferry dock via the Road of Liminality behind Youkai Mountain (or ~60 minutes via Muenzuka's border veil).
approach_route: Follow the Road of Liminality down the rear slope of Youkai Mountain into the permanent fog bank along the riverbank where Komachi Onozuka docks her ferry and Urumi Ushizaki raises prehistoric fish.
local_customs: Governed by the Ministry of Right and Wrong; living humans cannot swim across (the waters sink everything except shinigami boats) and must pay Komachi's ferry toll.

name_en: Higan & Ministry of Right and Wrong
short_desc: Eternal equinox flower plain on the far shore of the Sanzu River where Yama Eiki Shiki judges the dead.
long_desc: Located across the Sanzu River aboard Komachi's ferry, Higan is a tranquil, boundless plain of equinox blossoms where neither weather nor night exists. Here the Yama Eiki Shiki, Yamaxanadu holds court at the Ministry of Right and Wrong to assign souls to the Netherworld, Heaven, Hell, or reincarnation.
placement_note: Far western shore across the Sanzu River.
wiki_summary:
Higan () is the far side of the Sanzu River, where deceased souls wait for their turn to be judged by the Yama. It is possible to enter Hell and the Animal Realm through Higan as well. As a Pure Land, it has no weather, no seasons, and no night and day-- just an endless flower garden with a gentle warmth. It is strictly not part of Gensokyo.

Souls of the deceased will wait at the Shigan () (the shore of the living world) of the Sanzu River for a Shinigami to ferry them one at a time. As one gets to the Higan side, there is nothing to do but silently wait and contemplate death until the Yama is ready to pass judgement. The yama, who can see the souls' past, will judge whether they should go to the Netherworld, Heaven, Hell, or be reincarnated. If it's Hell, then the soul will fall outside the cycle of reincarnation temporarily.

The word "Higan" is composed of the kanji for that or over there () and shore (), so its literal meaning is "that shore" or "the shore on the other side". The Shigan (), which is located on the opposite end to the Higan, can literally mean "this shore" or "the shore on this side". Both of these term originate in Japanese Buddhism.
atlas_sector: Far Shore of the Sanzu River (eternal equinox plain where spirits await judgment).
travel_time: ~160–180 minutes total from the Human Village (~130 minutes to the Sanzu River dock + ~30 minutes ferry crossing aboard Komachi's boat).
approach_route: Reach the Sanzu River via the Road of Liminality and cross the fog-shrouded river on Komachi Onozuka's ferry to the flower-carpeted shore of Higan.
local_customs: Jurisdiction of Yama Eiki Shiki, Yamaxanadu; living visitors receive stern moral lectures and must depart before overstaying.

short_desc: Colossal sky gateway and endless stone staircase separating Gensokyo from the Netherworld.
long_desc: Standing at the top of a sweeping stone staircase in the clouds (linked spiritually to the Spring Path), the Barrier of Life and Death divides the realm of the living from the Netherworld. Ever since Yukari Yakumo thinned its boundary, approved visitors have been able to climb the stairs to Hakugyokurou.
placement_note: Threshold gate at the base of the Netherworld's grand stone staircase.
wiki_summary:
The Barrier of Life & Death (幽明結界, Yūmei Kekkai) is the boundary between Gensokyo and the Netherworld. Not much is known about the place.

The barrier itself is a giant door with four wooden pillars emerging from the clouds. Ever since the events of Perfect Cherry Blossom, the barrier has been weak because Yuyuko Saigyouji broke it to allow spring into the Netherworld. Thus, it is rather easy to enter the Netherworld, especially if you can fly. All you'd have to do is fly over the door, since it's locked. Yukari Yakumo was supposed to fix the barrier, but she never got around to it. However, this also means that phantoms can also leak into Gensokyo. According to Sakuya Izayoi's scenario of the said game, the location of the barrier is apparently not far from the Hakurei Shrine; on stage 3 after defeating Alice Margatroid, she says to go "upwind" in order to get to the barrier above the clouds, but going "downwind" will lead to the shrine.

The kanji does not have a clear meaning, but generally it refers to the afterlife (幽, Yuu) and the mortal world (明, mei). Therefore, a literal translation would be "The mortal realm and afterlife". Also, the kanji appears in Youmu Konpaku's spell cards Soul Sign "Wheel of Pain of the Living and Dead" (魂符「幽明の苦輪」) and Konpaku "Dharma of Gumonji Wisdom of the Living and Dead" (魂魄「幽明求聞持聡明の法」).
atlas_sector: Colossal Sky Gate separating Gensokyo's sky from the Netherworld.
travel_time: Reachable via flight above the Spring Path (~50 minutes SE of the Human Village to the Spring Path, then upward climb/flight up the endless stone stairs in the clouds).
approach_route: Ascend the cherry-blossom-lined Spring Path into the sky to the colossal doorway and climb the sweeping stone staircase into the Netherworld.
local_customs: Guarded boundary between the living world and the dead; weakened by Yukari Yakumo, allowing approved visitors to climb the stairs to Hakugyokurou.

short_desc: Serene cherry-blossom afterlife realm where sinless souls await reincarnation or nirvana.
long_desc: Beyond the Barrier of Life and Death lies a peaceful, pastel-lit afterlife of weeping cherry trees, stone bridges, and drifting white phantoms. Managed by Yuyuko Saigyouji and policed by half-phantom swordswoman Youmu Konpaku, it is one of Gensokyo's favorite spots for spring flower-viewing.
placement_note: Upper northern afterlife terrace beyond the Barrier of Life and Death.
wiki_summary:
The Netherworld (冥界, Meikai) is the land where ghosts and phantoms reside after death. After a phantom has been judged by the Yama, they'll either go to Hell, Heaven or to the Netherworld. The world frequently appears in various Touhou Project games and Manga, making it an important location.

The threat level in the Netherworld is 'high' and encounterable youkai include phantoms, ghosts and other types of spirits. After death, humans pass through the Road of Liminality, cross over the Sanzu River, and receive the Yama's judgement. Depending on the severity of their crimes, they are sent to either Hell, Heaven, or the Netherworld. Amongst these, the Netherworld is where the dead who aren't deemed sinful enough to be sent to Hell spend their time as phantoms, until they achieve Nirvana, and thus become able to enter Heaven, or reincarnate.

Different from the desolate Hell, the Netherworld is calm, though it has various seasons. It is filled with beautiful cherry blossoms in spring, and dyed with beautiful red leaves in autumn. The Netherworld is a notable place for people in the know for their cherry blossom viewing parties. The animals here are also dead, so they fly in the sky silently and splendidly. Like the Lunar Capital, it is a Pure Land where things do not change or decay with time; things from the Netherworld which seem old were simply made that way for aesthetic reasons.

Hakugyokurou, located in the Netherworld, is where two notable Touhou characters live: Youmu Konpaku and Yuyuko Saigyouji. The former is a gardener and the latter is the "princess" of the land. The manor is a beautiful structure, surrounded by walls and stairs using designs from the continent, and has a Japanese-style residence and Zen garden at its highest level. The entrance to the manor is a very long stairway called "Hakugyokurou's Stairway" (白玉楼階段, Hakugyokurou Kaidan).

Even though the dead comprise most of the Netherworld's inhabitants, the Netherworld is a distinct part of Gensokyo. However, travelling between the two is restricted by a gate above the clouds, sealed by the Barrier of Life & Death. During the main events of Perfect Cherry Blossom, a hole opened in the barrier between the Netherworld and Gensokyo, and it has become easier to travel between them. local_customs: Managed by Yuyuko Saigyouji and policed by Youmu Konpaku; wandering ghosts cluster around living trespassers unless escorted by Youmu.

short_desc: Yuyuko Saigyouji's aristocratic ghost estate and raked-stone cherry garden in the Netherworld.
long_desc: At the top of the Netherworld's grand stone staircase stands Hakugyokurou, a magnificent Japanese estate surrounded by raked gravel gardens and cherry orchards. Ghost princess Yuyuko Saigyouji and gardener-bodyguard Youmu Konpaku host seasonal banquets here.
placement_note: Crown estate of the Netherworld terrace.
wiki_summary:
Hakugyokurou (白玉楼) is a ghost shrine overlooking the Netherworld. It is well known among the afterlife realms for its cherry blossom gardens, and many ghosts come to see them every spring.

The term Hakugyokurou comes from Chinese legends of the Tang Dynasty (). It was said to be the place where artists go after death. Li He (), a poet from the Tang Dynasty, heard a voice in a dream he had as he was dying; the voice said, "Hakugyokurou has been completely built, so come and write down its details." The story is the beginning of Hakugyokurou.

Yuyuko Saigyouji is the lady of Hakugyokurou, and Youmu Konpaku acts as its gardener. The massive youkai cherry tree, the Saigyou Ayakashi, can also be found lying dormant in the gardens of Hakugyokurou.

Hakugyokurou was the location for stages 5 and 6 of Perfect Cherry Blossom, and several fights in Immaterial and Missing Power and Scarlet Weather Rhapsody.
atlas_sector: Central Ghost Shrine & Cherry Garden Estate inside the Netherworld.
travel_time: ~75 minutes from the Human Village via the Spring Path and the Netherworld's grand stone staircase.
approach_route: Ascend the sweeping stone steps past the Barrier of Life and Death to the traditional walled estate and cherry gardens housing the dormant Saigyou Ayakashi tree.
local_customs: Household of Yuyuko Saigyouji and Youmu Konpaku; guest access follows five centuries of Yuyuko's personal approvals, and every conversation is upstream of Yukari Yakumo's intelligence network.

long_desc: Towering over the innermost garden of Hakugyokurou, the Saigyou Ayakashi is a thousand-year-old youkai cherry tree whose blossoms once lured poets to peaceful death before it was sealed with Yuyuko Saigyouji's soul.
placement_note: Inner garden of Hakugyokurou.

local_customs: Household of Yuyuko Saigyouji and Youmu Konpaku; guest access follows five centuries of Yuyuko's personal approvals, and every conversation is upstream of Yukari Yakumo's intelligence network.

short_desc: Vast afterlife realm of judgment and punishment beyond Higan ruled by Goddess Hecatia Lapislazuli.
long_desc: Reorganized after the old subterranean Hell became overcrowded, New Hell is an immense otherworldly expanse connected to Higan's Ministry of Right and Wrong. Governed by three-bodied goddess Hecatia Lapislazuli, its burning plains are patrolled by kishin executives and stalked by Hisami Yomotsu.
first_appearance: TH15 / TH19 — Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost
placement_note: Northwest afterlife quadrant beyond Higan.
wiki_summary:
Hell (地獄, Jigoku), also New Hell (新地獄, Shin Jigoku), is a collection of realms separate from Gensokyo where sinful souls are imprisoned. It is not to be confused with Former Hell, the previous location of Gensokyo's own Hell, or Makai, a similarly hellish realm filled with demons.

Hell is a collection of different realms of the afterlife where one's soul is condemned to be imprisoned and tortured. Avici is one of many such realms, as was Former Hell in the past. Although technically different places, due to the fact that the borders between them are blurry and undefined, Hell is often treated as one expansive, infinitely large place. Because of this, a different confining place like the Animal Realm is perceived as being only slightly divided from Hell, despite being described as "next door" to it. Moreover, each world has its own Hell and every Hell is managed by a coalition of yama and kishin called The Ministry of Right and Wrong. Hell is one of many realms of the afterlife one may go to after being judged by a yama at Higan, with the other two major realms being Heaven and the Netherworld. 

[Basis]
The hell of Japanese mythology (地獄 Jigoku lit. "Earth Prison") is based on the Chinese mythological realm of the same name, pronounced "Diyu" and is not to be confused with the Shinto underworld, Yomi. Both hells are syntheses of the Buddhist Naraka, itself based on the Hindu Naraka, with traditional, pre-Buddhist beliefs. In Japan's tradition, souls must cross the Sanzu River to be judged at Higan. Souls are judged by ten judges known as the [https://www.onmarkproductions.com/html/sai-no-kawara.html#10kings Ten Kings of Hell] and are accordingly sent to whatever realm their lives' actions deserved. The main paths of the afterlife one may be sent to are called the [https://www.onmarkproductions.com/html/six-states.shtml Six Realms]. Hell is the lowest realm, being succeeded by the Preta Realm, Animal Realm, Human Realm, Asura Realm and Deva Realm, also known as Heaven. There are many Hells within Hell in Buddhism, with each having a specialized torture suited for every particular kind of sinner. One's time in Hell, as in the other five realms, is not eternal, however. It may take many millennia but souls eventually burn up all their negative karma and are reincarnated in a new realm, as is the eternal cycle of Samsara.

short_desc: Cutthroat cyberpunk-style metropolis in Hell ruled by warring beast-spirit yakuza syndicates.
long_desc: A ruthless concrete-and-neon realm adjacent to Hell where the law of the jungle reigns supreme. Three major beast-spirit organizations—Yachie Kicchou's Kiketsu Family, Saki Kurokoma's Keiga Family, and Yuuma Toutetsu's Gouyoku Alliance—wage eternal turf wars over enslaved human spirits.

placement_note: Far northwest afterlife sector adjacent to Higan and New Hell.
wiki_summary:
==General Information== 
The Animal Realm (畜生界, Chikushoukai) is a loosely-defined region of Hell (often treated as a separate neighboring realm) that is inhabited by countless animal spirits. As befits a realm related to Hell, the Animal Realm is a harsh place ruled by survival of the fittest, and human spirits are enslaved on the lowest rung of the animals' hierarchy.

While not directly connected to Gensokyo, it's possible to travel between the two by passing through greater Hell. The presence of border guards in Hell makes this difficult except during extenuating circumstances, however.

[Basis]
The Animal Realm is loosely based on the Tiryagyoni desire realm (畜生界, Chikushoukai) in real-world Buddhist cosmology, from where the in-universe location takes its name. In real-world Buddhist cosmology, the Tiryagyoni realm is the state of existence inhabited by non-human animals on Earth, and is distinct from the "Hell realm" of Naraka.

==Background Information== 

[Geography and People]
The majority of the Animal Realm is a skyscraper-filled metropolis, with one remaining forested region known as the Primate Spirit Garden where the human spirits are kept. The Garden is surrounded by a swamp, with its central island bearing a strong resemblance to the real-world Daisenryou Kofun, and is treated as a recreational area by the realm's animal inhabitants. During the events of Wily Beast and Weakest Creature, a high-tech fortress was built in the middle of the garden by Keiki Haniyasushin, but it may have been destroyed after her defeat.

The Animal Realm is ruled by three yakuza-esque gangs: Saki Kurokoma's Keiga Family, characterized by strength and brute force, Yachie Kicchou's Kiketsu Family, characterized by underhanded attacks from the shadows, Yuuma Toutetsu's Gouyoku Alliance, characterized by aerial warfare. 

Alongside these gangs exist many smaller, unnamed alliances which specialize in cowardly methods of attack such as traps, camouflage, and parasitism. It's said that survival in the Animal Realm practically necessitates working for one of these gangs.

[Names of the Groups]
The name of Yachie's family, the Kiketsu (鬼傑), roughly translates to "relentless excellence". 

The name of Saki's family, the Keiga (勁牙), translates to "strong fang". The character 勁 kei ("strong" or "agile") also appears in the prefix of most of her Spell Cards.

atlas_sector: Dystopian Metropolis & Wilderness Sector within Hell.
travel_time: Otherworldly realm adjacent to Hell (reachable via Hell boundary gates or spirit possession transit).

local_customs: Law of the jungle enforced by the Keiga Family (Saki Kurokoma), Kiketsu Family (Yachie Kicchou), and Gouyoku Alliance (Yuuma Toutetsu); unallied human spirits and visitors are enslaved on sight.

short_desc: Keyhole-shaped kofun burial mound fortress at the center of the Animal Realm defended by Keiki Haniyasushin.
long_desc: Originally a dismal reservation for human spirits inside the Animal Realm, this massive keyhole-shaped kofun park was transformed into an impenetrable idol fortress when the human spirits summoned sculptor goddess Keiki Haniyasushin and her terracotta Haniwa army.
first_appearance: TH17 — Wily Beast and Weakest Creature (2019)
placement_note: Central kofun fortress inside the Animal Realm.
wiki_summary:
The Primate Spirit Garden (霊長園, Reichouen) is a large park resembling a kofun burial mound, located in the Animal Realm. While it's typically a lush, natural location, part of it was transformed into a high-tech fortress by Keiki Haniyasushin during the events of Wily Beast and Weakest Creature.

==General Information== 
As the one major location in the Animal Realm that's lush with nature, the Garden is typically treated as a recreation spot by the resident animal spirits, as well as a place of captivity for the realm's human spirits. It bears a strong resemblance to the real-world Daisenryou Kofun, with a swamp surrounding the keyhole-shaped central island.

During Wily Beast and Weakest Creature, one of the Garden's main buildings was remodeled into a fortress by Keiki Haniyasushin as part of a hostile takeover to liberate the human spirits. The interior of the fortress is covered in holographic panels with a sci-fi aesthetic, featuring stylized icons of haniwa in certain places.

During the events of Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost, it is confirmed that a part of the Garden was liberated.
atlas_sector: Keyhole-Shaped Kofun Park & Fortress at the center of the Animal Realm.
travel_time: Central landmark within the Animal Realm metropolis.
approach_route: Navigate through the Animal Realm's concrete streets to the massive kofun burial mound park fortified by Keiki Haniyasushin's idol workshops.
local_customs: Fortified sanctuary of Keiki Haniyasushin and Mayumi Joutouguu's Haniwa Army Corps; protects human spirits against the outer beast syndicates, though Keiki's protection is intensely possessive.

short_desc: Steaming geyser cavern at the foot of Youkai Mountain that descends into the Underworld.
long_desc: Situated a 50-minute walk north of the Human Village at the rocky base of Youkai Mountain, the Fantastic Blowhole is the primary surface cavern leading down into the Underworld. Earth spider Yamame Kurodani and bucket-youkai Kisume haunt its steaming upper shafts.
placement_note: Surface-to-Underworld cavern mouth at the southern base of Youkai Mountain.
wiki_summary: The Fantastic Blowhole (幻想風穴, Gensō Kazaana) is a gloomy cave that leads further into the Underworld, where the next layer after here is the Deep Road to Hell. Apart from the known fact that Kisume and Yamame Kurodani are known to lurk around here, there is not much known about this place, nor is its location in Gensokyo. Apparently, the hole is soaking wet, and the wind that comes through here is strong. Rocks are also known to tumble down here.
atlas_sector: Surface-to-Underworld Cavern Entrance at the base of Youkai Mountain.
travel_time: ~50–60 minutes walk north from the Human Village North Gate to the geyser cave mouth.
approach_route: Follow the foothills trail at the base of Youkai Mountain to the steaming rocky cavern where Yamame Kurodani and Kisume linger near the shaft drop.
local_customs: Threshold to the Underworld frequented by Yamame Kurodani and Kisume; requires light and cold/heat preparation before descending.

name_en: Deep Road to Hell & Parsee's Bridge
short_desc: Vertical subterranean shaft and green-lit bridge guarded by bridge princess Parsee Mizuhashi.
long_desc: Plunging from the Fantastic Blowhole down toward the cavern ceiling of Former Hell, the Deep Road to Hell ends at an ancient wooden bridge spanning the abyss. Hashihime Parsee Mizuhashi watches over travelers crossing between the surface and the Underworld.
placement_note: Upper gateway shaft of the Underworld cartouche.
wiki_summary: The Deep Road to Hell (地獄の深道, Jigoku no fukadō) is a gloomy hole that continues from the Fantastic Blowhole that leads further into the Underworld, where the next layer after here is the Former Capital in Former Hell. Apart from the known fact that Parsee Mizuhashi, the bridge princess, is known to lurk around here, there is not much known about this place, nor is its location in Gensokyo as a whole. Parsee describes this place as an "underground skyscraper". A bridge is known to be located here, as both described in-game and shown on Wild and Horned Hermit Chapter 2.
atlas_sector: Vertical Subterranean Shaft & Bridge linking the Fantastic Blowhole to Former Hell.
travel_time: ~75 minutes from the Human Village (~50 min to the Fantastic Blowhole + ~25 min descent to the bridge).
approach_route: Descend the gloomy green-lit rock shaft beneath the Fantastic Blowhole and cross the subterranean bridge guarded by Parsee Mizuhashi.
local_customs: Guarded by hashihime Parsee Mizuhashi, who feeds on travelers' jealousy along the bridge crossing.

short_desc: Self-governed subterranean realm beneath Gensokyo inhabited by oni, satori, and underground youkai.
long_desc: Sealed off by mutual non-interference treaties with the surface sages, the Underworld is a vast subterranean cavern system deep beneath Youkai Mountain. Disliked surface youkai, ancient oni, and vengeful spirits live here in rugged autonomy.
placement_note: Main subterranean realm basin in the Underworld cartouche.
wiki_summary:
The Underworld ( chitei, underground) is a world beneath the surface of Gensokyo, and consists of many regions. It is the main focus of the plot of Subterranean Animism. It's suggested that it's a separate world from Gensokyo.

The Underworld is made up of several different layers. The uppermost one, which is still very far below ground, is known as Old Hell, which was once Hell long ago, before the Yamas decided to relocate due to overpopulation. The Old Capital and the Palace of the Earth Spirits are located on this layer, supposedly at the center of what used to be Hell.

Below that, accessed via a hole in the courtyard of the Palace of the Earth Spirits, is the Remains of Blazing Hell, which produces the heat for Old Hell. Below even that lies the Nuclear Furnace, seen in Stage 6 of Subterranean Animism, which is kept alight by Utsuho Reiuji, and functions the main power source for the rest of the Underworld. Even lower is the Hell of Blood Pools, where the emotions of countless organisms congeal as blood that can be perceived as oil. 

[Underground Geyser Center]

The Underground Geyser Center is also located below ground, at the foot of the Youkai Mountain. This experimentation center set up by Kanako Yasaka and Suwako Moriya connects to the Nuclear Furnace.
atlas_sector: Subterranean Realm deep beneath Youkai Mountain and Gensokyo.
travel_time: ~90–120 minutes total descent from the Human Village (~45–60 min walk to the Fantastic Blowhole or Rainbow Cavern entrance + ~45–60 min vertical/tunnel descent).
approach_route: Enter via the Fantastic Blowhole at the foot of Youkai Mountain or the Rainbow Cavern of Earth Spirits -> descend through the Deep Road to Hell past Parsee's bridge into Former Hell.
local_customs: Self-governed subterranean society of oni (Yuugi), satori (Satori, Koishi), and disliked underground youkai; surface treaties forbid topside interference.

short_desc: Rowdy Edo-styled subterranean city ruled by oni Yuugi Hoshiguma beneath the Deep Road bridge.
long_desc: Once the bureaucratic capital of Hell before the Ministry relocated across the Sanzu River, the Old Capital is now a bustling, snow-dusted subterranean town of wooden bridges, sake taverns, and lantern-lit streets where Yuugi Hoshiguma and her fellow oni revel.
placement_note: Central city cavern of the Underworld.
wiki_summary:
The Old Capital (旧都, Kyuuto) is a large village in Old Hell, deep within the Underworld. It is situated between the Deep Road to Hell, guarded by Parsee Mizuhashi, and the Palace of the Earth Spirits, where the sisters Satori Komeiji and Koishi Komeiji live.

The buildings appear to be modelled after traditional Japanese houses, and the streets appear to be lit with fiery hanging lanterns. Although the city is built underground, it is still able to receive snowfall.

The capital is populated primarily by oni, who moved underground long ago as part of a deal with the yamas. After promising to keep a lid on the vengeful spirits that remained there after the yama relocated Hell, the oni were given permission to stay there. As such, many oni, such as Yuugi Hoshiguma, can easily be found partying in the streets here. Suika Ibuki visits here from time to time. Aside from the oni, many other subterranean youkai can probably be found here on occasions, as Yamame Kurodani mentions that the city doesn't turn away visitors.
atlas_sector: Main Subterranean City Cavern in the Underworld (beneath the Deep Road to Hell).
travel_time: ~90–100 minutes walk/descent from the Human Village via the Fantastic Blowhole and Deep Road to Hell.
approach_route: Cross Parsee's bridge at the bottom of the Deep Road to Hell into the Edo-styled subterranean streets of Former Hell and Hot Spring Town.
local_customs: Rowdy subterranean territory ruled by oni Yuugi Hoshiguma and administered from the Palace of the Earth Spirits by Satori Komeiji; physical strength and blunt honesty are respected.

short_desc: Steaming subterranean bathhouse resort district in Former Hell warmed by the fires below.
long_desc: Fed by geothermal springs heated by the Remains of Blazing Hell, this lively bathhouse quarter in Former Hell attracts both underground oni and bold surface visitors looking to soak in mineral waters and share sake cups.
placement_note: Resort quarter adjacent to the streets of Former Hell.
wiki_summary:
Old Hell's Hot Spring Town (旧地獄温泉街, Kyū-jigoku onsen-gai) is a resort district in Old Hell, deep within the Underworld. It is accessible from the Rainbow Cavern of Earth Spirits, and managed by Yuugi Hoshiguma.

The buildings are tall and densely-packed, and appear to be modelled after traditional Japanese houses. What appears to be steam or hot water continually pours down from above. The buildings are interspersed with large hot springs, in which oni and vengeful spirits can be seen bathing.
atlas_sector: Resort District of Former Hell in the Underworld.
travel_time: ~90 minutes from the Human Village via the Fantastic Blowhole and Deep Road to Hell (or via the Hakurei Shrine hot-spring geyser fissure).
approach_route: Enter Former Hell past the Deep Road bridge and follow the lantern-lit streets to the steaming subterranean bathhouses where Yuugi Hoshiguma drinks.
local_customs: Neutral subterranean resort district where oni and surface visitors drink and bathe under Yuugi's watch.

short_desc: Satori Komeiji's stained-glass Gothic mansion built directly atop the vent of Blazing Hell.
long_desc: Standing in the central plaza of Former Hell, the Palace of the Earth Spirits is an ornate Western mansion with rose-patterned stained glass windows and ironwork grates in its courtyard floor. From here, mind-reading mistress Satori Komeiji and her pets Rin Kaenbyou and Utsuho Reiuji manage the sealed inferno below.
placement_note: Central administrative mansion of Former Hell.
wiki_summary:
The Palace of the Earth Spirits (地霊殿, Chireiden) is a mansion situated in the center of what used to be Hell (now Old Hell) in the Underworld, and is near the Old Capital.

The palace is a Western-style mansion with what appears to be many stained glass windows on a chequered floor. According to Symposium of Post-mysticism, the floors of the palace are heated. In the courtyard is a large hole that leads to the Hell of Blazing Fires below. It's said that the palace was constructed after the Underworld was separated from Hell. 

Satori Komeiji took control of the palace and managed it by herself with the help of her pets, keeping it relatively peaceful. Of her pets, Rin Kaenbyou's duty is to carry corpses to the Remains of Blazing Hell for the heating of Old Hell and Utsuho Reiuji is to maintain that heat. The other pets' duties were said to be tending the garden and playing with Satori's sister, Koishi Komeiji.
atlas_sector: Central Mansion of Former Hell (stained-glass western estate sitting directly above the Remains of Blazing Hell).
travel_time: ~100–110 minutes total travel from the Human Village (~90 min to Former Hell + ~15 min through the subterranean streets to the central courtyard).
approach_route: Walk through the streets of Former Hell past Hot Spring Town to the stained-glass western mansion at the cavern's center.
local_customs: Household of Satori Komeiji, Koishi Komeiji, Rin Kaenbyou (Orin), and Utsuho Reiuji (Okuu); Satori's third eye reads visitors' minds immediately upon entry.

short_desc: Scorching subterranean cauldron beneath Chireiden tended by kasha Rin Kaenbyou and Hell Ravens.
long_desc: Directly beneath the courtyard grates of the Palace of the Earth Spirits plunges a colossal cavern of magma rivers, iron catwalks, and swirling vengeful spirits. Kasha Rin Kaenbyou wheels her cart of corpses through the heat to fuel the fires below.
placement_note: Deep vertical furnace cavern directly beneath the Palace of the Earth Spirits.
wiki_summary:
The Remains of Blazing Hell (灼熱地獄跡, Shakunetsu Jigoku Ato), also known as the Hell of Blazing Fires (灼熱地獄, Shakunetsu Jigoku) and Remains of Hell (地獄跡地, Jigoku Atochi), is thought to be in the deepest part of the Underworld, located below Former Hell and the Palace of the Earth Spirits.

The Remains of Blazing Hell was formerly a part of Former Hell where criminals were banished, it has recently been re-ignited because of the activation of the Nuclear Furnace directly below by Utsuho Reiuji. Rin Kaenbyou can be found here, carting corpses into the Furnace to keep it running. The place is very hot because it has a lot of magma. It is infested with vengeful spirits. Since people stopped being condemned to the hellfires, the oni don't visit any more either, so this place has become the playground to such spirits and animals. It's said that if you die here, your corpse will be trapped here and you'll turn into a vengeful spirit, where you cannot make it to Heaven regardless of your innocence.

Before the events of Subterranean Animism, the Blazing Fires were apparently not as hot as it is now, because when Hell moved to a new location that in itself created Former Hell, the Blazing Fires started to cool down, thus becoming dark, and Satori Komeiji sealed it off with the Palace of the Earth Spirits. Thus, this became space for Kanako Yasaka and Suwako Moriya to start a Mountain Industrial Revolution project, and Utsuho burned it up again after she swallowed the god Yatagarasu.
atlas_sector: Deep Subterranean Inferno directly beneath the Palace of the Earth Spirits.
travel_time: ~120 minutes total descent from the Human Village (~100 min to the Palace of the Earth Spirits + ~15–20 min down the vertical furnace shafts).
approach_route: Pass through the courtyard of the Palace of the Earth Spirits and descend the scorching vertical shafts tended by Rin Kaenbyou and Hell Ravens.
local_customs: Extreme thermal hazard zone patrolled by Orin, Utsuho Reiuji, and vengeful spirits; unshielded humans will succumb to heatstroke within minutes.

name_en: Hell of Blazing Fires Nuclear Furnace
short_desc: Subterranean fusion reactor core regulated by hell raven Utsuho Reiuji at the bottom of Blazing Hell.
long_desc: Constructed at the lowest floor of the Remains of Blazing Hell as part of Kanako Yasaka's Mountain Industrial Revolution Project, the Nuclear Furnace harnesses the sun-god Yatagarasu within Utsuho Reiuji to supply clean geothermal and fusion energy to Youkai Mountain.
placement_note: Lowest core beneath the Remains of Blazing Hell.
wiki_summary:
The Nuclear Furnace (核融合炉, Kakuyuugouro) is a super-high furnace that's used for high-temperature heating in an attempt to tame a power that the Outside World apparently won't master for hundreds of years: nuclear fusion energy. It is located at one of the deepest layers of the Underworld, just below the Remains of Blazing Hell but one layer above the Hell of Blood Pools.

It produces the heat and power for the Former Hell and it's connected to the Underground Geyser Center via a very long passageway. Utsuho Reiuji can be found here to power it and Rin Kaenbyou carts corpses into the Furnace to keep it running. Kanako Yasaka and Suwako Moriya were looking for a high temperature, high pressure furnace to revolutionize the kappa's energy production and thus made use of the Remains of Blazing Hell due to it not being used and Utsuho helped them to create the Furnace. It's now being utilized by the kappa of the Youkai Mountain as part of their Mountain Industrial Revolution project. In Wild and Horned Hermit, Kanako and Suwako attempt to develop a better version of the nuclear fusion, probably as a way to convert the current Nuclear Furnace into something more efficient. It used to lie dormant but because of the plans of Kanako Yasaka and Suwako Moriya, it is now fully active.
atlas_sector: Deepest Core of the Remains of Blazing Hell beneath the Palace of the Earth Spirits.
travel_time: ~135 minutes total descent from the Human Village (at the very bottom of the Remains of Blazing Hell).
approach_route: Descend to the lowest floor of the Remains of Blazing Hell into the reactor chamber regulated by Utsuho Reiuji.
local_customs: Regulated by Utsuho Reiuji under Moriya Shrine's energy project; lethal temperatures and radiation bursts require magical or kappa shielding.

short_desc: Kappa-engineered subterranean maintenance conduit linking Youkai Mountain to the Nuclear Furnace.
long_desc: Accessible via an elevator shaft on Youkai Mountain or through the side tunnels of the Nuclear Furnace, this steel-and-brick industrial facility lets Kappa engineers monitor pressure pipes and thermal output from Utsuho's reactor.
placement_note: Engineering conduit adjacent to the Nuclear Furnace.
wiki_summary: The Underground Geyser Center (間欠泉地下センター, kanketsusen-chika sentaa) is a facility under the surface of Gensokyo, under the base of the Youkai Mountain. Both the kappa and the gods at the Moriya Shrine perform a variety of experiments and research projects. It is connected to the Nuclear Furnace in the deepest part of the Underworld.
atlas_sector: Subterranean Engineering Conduit linking Youkai Mountain / Moriya Shrine to the Nuclear Furnace.
travel_time: ~90–120 minutes descent from Youkai Mountain's geyser shafts (or adjacent to the Nuclear Furnace below the Palace of the Earth Spirits).
approach_route: Enter via the maintenance elevator shaft on Youkai Mountain or through the side tunnels of the Nuclear Furnace.
local_customs: Restricted Kappa and Moriya Shrine industrial facility; unauthorized entry triggers automated defense drones and Utsuho's patrols.

short_desc: Abyssal black-oil ocean beneath Blazing Hell controlled by Yuuma Toutetsu and the Gouyoku Alliance.
long_desc: Located in the deepest pitch-black strata below the Remains of Blazing Hell, this subterranean sea of crude black water—distilled from the ancient dregs of the Hell of Blood Pools—is harvested by taotie matriarch Yuuma Toutetsu.
placement_note: Abyssal stratum beneath the Remains of Blazing Hell.
atlas_sector: Abyssal Subterranean Stratum beneath the Remains of Blazing Hell.
travel_time: ~150 minutes descent from the surface into the deep oil-filled caverns below the Nuclear Furnace.
approach_route: Descend past the Remains of Blazing Hell into the deepest pitch-black oil caverns where Yuuma Toutetsu and the Gouyoku Alliance harvest black-water energy.
local_customs: Controlled by Yuuma Toutetsu and the Gouyoku Alliance; toxic fumes and predatory spirits make it lethal to ordinary humans.

long_desc: The deepest, most lawless basin of Old Hell where boiling crimson pools of condensed sin bubble alongside the Sea of Petroleum. Tenkajin Chiyari and Yuuma Toutetsu lurk within its toxic, miasma-choked caverns.
first_appearance: TH17.5 / TH19 — Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost
placement_note: Deepest abyssal basin at the bottom of the Underworld cartouche.

The Hell of Blood Pools or the Old Hell's Blood Pools (旧血の池地獄, Kyuu Chinoike Jigoku) is a place situated in the Old Hell, below the Remains of Blazing Hell.

The Hell of Blood Pools is considered the most unpleaseant area of Old Hell, a place where the energy of the wicked spirits are chipped away and which eventually absorbs the wicked spirits themselves into the sea of blood. This Hell was considered so bad, even for Old Hell standards, that few Oni wanted to take care it, leaving the place unmanageable. After the relocation to New Hell, the Hell of Blood Pools was deliberately completely forgotten and abandoned by the inhabitants of Old Hell.

travel_time: ~150 minutes descent from the surface into the crimson sin-pool basin beside the Sea of Petroleum.
approach_route: Follow the deepest subterranean fissures past the Remains of Blazing Hell and the Sea of Petroleum into the crimson sin-pool caverns.
local_customs: Haunted by Chiyari Tenkajin, Yuuma Toutetsu, and lingering sinners; completely lawless abyssal zone.

short_desc: Sealed demon dimension of thick magical miasma created by Goddess Shinki.
long_desc: Accessible via the sealed mountain cave behind the Hakurei Shrine or by flying the Palanquin Ship through Hokkai's dimensional rift, Makai is a bizarre otherworld saturated with dense magical energy that empowers witches like Byakuren and Alice while poisoning unshielded mortals.

placement_note: Western otherworld cartouche connected to the Hakurei mountain cave and Myouren Palanquin route.
wiki_summary:
Makai (魔界) is a world that exists separate from Gensokyo. In the past works of PC-98, it was created by Shinki. It is not to be confused with Hell (地獄, jigoku) as it is not an afterlife realm that phantoms go to after being judged by the yama, but merely a place where demons and strong youkai live.

Makai's first initial appearance in the Touhou Project was in the first PC-98 game Highly Responsive to Prayers, where it is one of the main locations of the game. It then appeared as the prime location of Mystic Square, where the player character will have an adventure through here. After many years of absence, Makai once again made a return in the Windows era as the location of Stages 5 and 6 in Undefined Fantastic Object, and again as a target location on Stages 7 and 12 in Double Spoiler.

Due to the canonicity between the PC-98 and the Windows era, Makai has somewhat mixed information. ZUN has stated that he wanted a "clean sweep" from the PC-98 when he was creating new games for Windows, but he also explicitly stated that the settings for the PC-98 and Windows are essentially the same, thus Makai from both the PC-98 and Windows ought to also be the same. However, he does also say to take reference from the Windows era of the Touhou Project to consider what is canon. Hence, information is split into two as followed:

;In PC-98
The entrance to Makai is located in the mountains behind the Hakurei Shrine, called the {{nihongo|"Cave in Which the Door to Makai is Said to Be" and a portal appeared at the Hakurei Shrine in Highly Responsive to Prayers.

Makai was shown to have many demons and even spirits, where it was said that everything within Makai was created by Shinki, the God of this world. It is filled with gloom and darkness, where flying through here can give the feeling of being outer space, but there are also extensive fields of crystalline forests and frozen fields. There appears to be no natural material such as flowers. Louise, a resident here, describes Makai as a "nice place". It is filled with a toxic miasma that's physically harmful that makes it impossible to get to Makai, but it strengthens magical spells and seals, and it can also make learning magic easier for a human. Apart from Byakuren formerly, no known character from the Windows era lives here. There is no history about this place, and it is unknown where it's located.

wiki_summary:
The Dream World (夢の世界, Yume no Sekai) is a world that is visited via dreaming and is ruled by Doremy Sweet.

The Dream World is normally accessed via dreams, where the dreamer exists as their "dream self".

In Legacy of Lunatic Kingdom, the Dream World is mysteriously accessed physically through a secret passageway that Reisen Udongein Inaba calls "Kaian Passageway #4 (第四槐安通路)", and is said to be used as a method of travel between the Lunar Capital and Gensokyo by the moon rabbits. The passageway seems to resemble outer space somewhat, as Sanae Kochiya exclaims "I'm flying through space!", and both the Moon and a purple Earth are visible, seen in Stage 3 and the Extra Stage respectively.

There is no information suggesting the Fantasy World (夢幻世界) in Lotus Land Story, the World of Fantasies (幻夢界) in Story of Eastern Wonderland, or Mugetsu's world, are at all related.
atlas_sector: Astral Collective Unconscious Dimension spanning between Gensokyo, the Outside World, and the Moon.
travel_time: Instantaneous during sleep (or reachable physically via Doremy Sweet's dream gates / Yukari's boundary gaps).
approach_route: Enter through sleep or cross a dream-boundary portal managed by baku ruler Doremy Sweet.
local_customs: Managed and policed by Doremy Sweet; dream-selves behave without waking inhibitions, and lingering physically in the Dream World risks psychic displacement.

short_desc: Barren cratered surface of the Moon and the Sea of Tranquility guarding the Lunar Veil.
long_desc: Connected to Gensokyo via the Dream World's Lunar Passage, full-moon lake reflections, and the Asama Purifying Mountain corridor, the Sea of Tranquility is the outer lunar battlefield patrolled by Seiran, Ringo, and the Lunar Defense Corps.
placement_note: Outer ring of the northeast Lunar Cartouche.

wiki_summary: The Sea of Tranquility (静かの海, Shizuka no Umi) or Sea of Tranquillity (see Latin is a lunar mare, a large and dark plain that's located on the Near Side of the Moon (月の表側), to the east of the Sea of Serenity and to the west of the Sea of Prosperity.

travel_time: Interplanetary / Metaphysical distance (reachable only via the Lunar Veil reflection on Misty Lake during a full moon, the Dream World's Lunar Passage, or the Asama Purifying Mountain portal).
approach_route: Travel through the Dream World's Lunar Capital passage, cross the full-moon reflection barrier, or use the hidden Sea of Tranquility corridor inside Asama Purifying Mountain.
local_customs: Patrolled by the Lunar Defense Corps and moon rabbits; Earthlings are considered impure and shot on sight without Lunarian clearance.

short_desc: Pure, barrier-veiled metropolis on the far side of the Moon ruled by Lord Tsukuyomi and the Watatsuki sisters.
long_desc: Hidden behind a veil of purity on the far side of the Moon alongside a tranquil lunar sea and peach orchards, the Lunar Capital is an immortal civilization engineered by Lord Tsukuyomi and Eirin Yagokoro, defended by Watatsuki no Toyohime, Yorihime, and Sagume Kishin.
placement_note: Center of the northeast Lunar Cartouche.
wiki_summary:
The Lunar Capital (月の都, Tsuki no Miyako), or Lunatic Kingdom (ルナティックキングダム, Runatikku Kingudamu), is a thriving, ancient metropolis and currently the only known one on the Moon, located on its far side. With its civilisation mostly having Lunarians and Moon Rabbits, its technology and weaponry is known to be far more advanced than that of the Outside World. The founder and lord of the capital is Lord Tsukuyomi.

The Lunar Capital is also the legendary Dragon Palace (竜宮, Ryūgū), also called the Dragon King's Palace (竜宮城, Ryūgū-jō), that Mizue no Uranoshimako managed to reach, but it doesn't seem to be common knowledge since characters such as Rinnosuke Morichika still think of the Dragon Palace as a completely different place on the bottom of the sea.

The capital is protected by a barrier that hides its existence., presumably because of this barrier. Like Gensokyo, it thus could effectively be considered another world. The capital is shown to have skyscrapers Some records from the Genso-Lunar War are still intact which even go so far as to detail the weapons the lunarians had back then, Even in the near future of Maribel Hearn and Renko Usami's time, the idea of a Lunar Capital is still just a legend, although Maribel herself is able to see the Lunar Capital due to her ability to see through boundaries.

Although the Lunar Capital is protected by a barrier, things such as humans planting a flag on the Moon or colonizing it still presents a major problem for unspecified reasons. It is serious enough that humanity planting a flag and simply attempting to establish bases on the moon is referred to as the "Lunar War" and their failure to do so considered a "defeat". For both that past invasion and the one taking place in the present day, actual combat is being heavily considered due to humanity's attempts to establish bases on the Moon. or using a Sanctuary as a passageway.
atlas_sector: Barrier-Veiled Metropolis on the Far Side of the Moon.

wiki_summary:
Gensokyo (幻想郷, gensoukyou is the setting of Touhou Project. Its culture vaguely resembles that of feudal Japan, heavily embellished with folkloric elements.

Gensokyo is a remote place, far from any human habitation. In ancient times, this place was densely populated by youkai and those humans who wandered too close would be eaten by them. Most people feared the youkai, but a brave warrior would occasionally rise to defeat them. Some of those brave humans settled in Gensokyo to keep close watch on the youkai. Scientific advancements among the human race further contributed to Gensokyo's growing human minority. Due to this, Yukari Yakumo implemented a plan roughly 500 years ago to restore the power of youkai in Gensokyo by creating a "Barrier that divides Reality and Fantasy" called the Youkai Expansion Project. With the plan's implementation, Gensokyo became a place that attracted things that have become fantasy outside; in other words, things that were forgotten in the Outside World such as youkai, lost items, and such are paranormally transported into Gensokyo. In 1885 A.D., Gensokyo was again made isolated from the rest of Earth with the creation of the Great Hakurei Barrier. Gensokyo has made next to no attempt at contact with the outside world since its creation. Gensokyo's language is modern Japanese.

[Geography]

Gensokyo, the area encompassed by the Great Hakurei Barrier, is a landlocked territory comprised mainly of forested mountains. Notable geographic features include the Youkai Mountain with communities of kappa at its base, tengu at its peak, and the Moriya Shrine at a lake near the top; the Forest of Magic; the Bamboo Forest of the Lost where Eientei is located; the Misty Lake next to the Scarlet Devil Mansion; the Human Village and adjacent Myouren Temple, which are assumed to be in a fertile valley; the Sanzu River separating Gensokyo from Higan; and the Hakurei Shrine at the east of Gensokyo.

Although passing through the Hakurei Barrier to the Outside World is normally impossible for most humans and youkai, stronger entities are known to be able to pass through. It is also significantly easier for Gensokyo denizens to access domains of gods, demons, and spirits which are not strictly part of Gensokyo itself. These include Higan, the Netherworld, Makai, Heaven, Senkai, the Moon, and the Underworld.

TORIFUNE was designed as a self-contained ecosystem of hardy plants and animals, in order to gather data to be used for terraforming parts of Earth. Possibly due to its resemblance to Noah's Ark, the station was named after Ame-no-Torifune (a kami of ships) and a shrine to him was built inside.

Control of the station was lost a few years before the events of Trojan Green Asteroid due to a mysterious computer bug, but an automated system moved it to rest safely at a Lagrangian point between the Earth and Moon. Since retrieving it would be difficult, and all life aboard was presumed dead, contact with the station has not been made since then. Critics said "Japan's engineers have spent a large sum of money just to make a ruin in space".

In truth, the station's interior has become an overgrown jungle, while some of its animal species have mutated into chimerae.

Uwabami note
The Twilight Bar Room (黄昏酒場, Tasogare sakaba) is where all of Uwabami Breakers take place. Apart from this game, nothing else official in existence has made reference to this place. The name also appears as the Japanese title of the game.
